500307|2026-06.headline: Nirlon Q1 FY27: total income Rs.173 crore (+3% YoY), EBITDA Rs.134 crore (+1%), PAT about Rs.69 crore (+19%), occupancy 99.8%.
500307|2026-06.overview: Nirlon reported Q1 FY27 total income of about Rs.173 crore (+3% YoY), EBITDA of Rs.134 crore (+1% YoY, 77.30% margin) and PAT of about Rs.69 crore (+19% YoY, 40.19% margin). Average occupancy across NKP and Nirlon House was 99.8%, with about 6,900 sq ft vacant at June 30, 2026. Management said FY27 is a quiet year for lease expiries and rental growth will come mainly from contracted escalations; no tenant additions were made in the quarter. On REIT conversion, Nirlon House redevelopment and GIC-related talks, management gave no new substantive update.

financial_highlights.change: Management described it as moderating sequentially per analyst; no YoY figure stated

segments.name: NKP (Nirlon Knowledge Park)
segments.commentary: Operating leases are fully contracted; management expects no significant new additions in Q1 FY27 and no major lease expiries in FY27. Routine capex only for upgrades to Grade A standard.

segments.name: Nirlon House
segments.commentary: Leased about 1,100 sq ft office in Q1 at roughly Rs.250 per sq ft per month (analyst's figure; management confirmed approx). Building has 12 other co-owners, so redevelopment needs their consent and no update was given.

guidance_outlook: Rental growth for rest of FY27 to come predominantly from contracted escalations under existing leave and licence agreements; no significant growth outside contracts expected.
Annual escalations of about 4.75% (plus or minus a few basis points), replacing the earlier 15% every three years structure.
EBITDA margins expected to stay steady, based on existing contracts; management hopes to maintain and improve them.
Debt repayment starts May 2027: 5% per year, totalling 25%, under the existing lender agreement.
Management declined to guide on FY27 dividend or on net debt trajectory (analyst asked about moving to about 1.5 from 1.8).
No decision on prepaying debt; no serious discussion with lenders yet.
capex_capacity: Only routine capex planned at NKP for upgrades and maintenance to keep the park at international Grade A standard; no redevelopment or expansion announced.
No new capacity or commissioning timelines were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Management says occupancy is essentially full, so live or serious inquiries are few; demand is going elsewhere in the Goregaon/western suburbs micro market.
Management views rentals as competitive but declined to compare them with other Goregaon assets, citing differences in efficiency, rent-free periods, deposits and escalations.
GCC growth described as a positive driver of Mumbai and Maharashtra office demand; no quantified data given.
Old-building carpet-to-chargeable efficiency at Nirlon House about 95-100%.

qa_highlights.question: Any plan to convert to a REIT, given the tax amendment for REIT dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no concrete plans to convert to a REIT and it will disclose any significant structural change.

qa_highlights.question: Any progress on redeveloping Nirlon House?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said redevelopment needs consent from 12 other co-owners, takes significant time, and there is nothing significant to report.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company prepay debt given healthy cash?
qa_highlights.answer: No decision has been taken and no serious discussion has happened with lenders on prepayment.

qa_highlights.question: How should rental growth look for the rest of FY27, and are there lease expiries?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth will follow contracts; FY27 is described as a fairly quiet year with no significant expiries and nothing heard from larger licensees to suggest otherwise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did licence-fee income grow only 0.9% QoQ, and will EBITDA margins hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to contracted licences with escalations timing; it hopes margins hold, expecting only steady fluctuation based on contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 dividend rose to Rs.30 per share from Rs.26, but it would not comment on FY27 dividend, which has not been discussed internally.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt trajectory and restructuring progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to speculate on net debt numbers and said there is nothing significant to report on GIC or Nirlon House talks.

risks_watch: Growth is capped by fully contracted, nearly full occupancy; no new leasing upside visible in FY27.
Debt amortisation starts May 2027 (5% a year, 25% total), which may affect EBITDA margins and leverage; the analyst cited net debt of 1.81.
No dividend guidance for FY27 after the Rs.30 FY26 payout; watch for the interim and final dividend announcements.
Nirlon House redevelopment and REIT conversion remain unresolved; co-owner consent needed.
Licence-fee growth slowed to 0.9% QoQ; the next quarter will show whether escalations flow through.
Management gave no ETA for an average remaining lease tenure figure, which was withheld on the call.
500307|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on occupancy and contracted rentals but noticeably cautious and evasive on forward items: REIT, Nirlon House, GIC talks, dividend, net debt and lease tenure all got non-committal answers.

So, basically, we of course are trying to get as much information and details, etc., with regards to GCCs, because GCCs, as you know, are a very good source, are a very important source of real estate demand in Mumbai, Maharashtra, as well as in India.
26-27 is a fairly quiet year in terms of any significant leave and license agreements expiring or getting off in terms of any of the existing leave and license agreements expiring.

rows.why: Management said there are no concrete REIT plans and nothing significant to report on Nirlon House, which needs consent from 12 co-owners and takes significant time.

rows.why: Management said no decision has been taken and no serious lender discussion has happened, despite healthy cash; the analyst cited net debt of 1.81 and asked about a move to about 1.5.

500325|2026-03.headline: Reliance Q4 FY26: consolidated EBITDA flat YoY as Oil-to-Chemicals fell 4%, while Jio and Retail grew 14% combined; FY26 EBITDA up 13.5%.
500325|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a quarter of severe energy shock from the Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, with crude premiums, freight and insurance costs sharply higher and refinery throughput down 4% YoY to 19.5 MMT-equivalent (as stated). Consumer businesses (Jio and Retail) drove growth, with Jio Platforms FY26 EBITDA of Rs 76,255 Crores (around 19% YoY) and Retail record quarterly revenue of Rs 98,000 Crores. Quarterly PAT was pressured by higher depreciation and interest from 5G asset capitalisation. Management said Jio IPO is "fairly imminent" and gave no hard numbers on targets or margins beyond the stated trends.

financial_highlights.metric: Group FY26 EBITDA growth (includes one-time gain on sale of listed shares)

segments.name: Jio Platforms / Connectivity (RJIL)
segments.commentary: Ended FY26 with 524.4 mn subscribers (net add 9.1 mn in quarter); 268 mn 5G users (+77 mn in year); 27 mn fixed broadband homes, 75% via JioAirFiber. ARPU Rs 214, up 4% YoY with no tariff action; data per capita 42.3 GB/month.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Record Q4 revenue Rs 98,000 Crores (+11% YoY, ~14% ex-RCPL); EBITDA Rs 6,900 Crores at 7.9% margin, margin diluted by hyperlocal growth. Hyperlocal average daily orders +300% YoY; store count crossed 20,000 with 333 openings in the quarter.

segments.name: FMCG (Reliance Consumer Products)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 22,000 Crores; Q4 Rs 7,350 Crores, roughly 2x YoY. Campa brand Rs 4,700 Crores; Independence Rs 2,600 Crores; present in 40 countries; acquired Goodness Group (Australia) and Manna (millets).

segments.name: JioStar
segments.commentary: Monthly active user reach of 550 mn in March; T20 World Cup peak concurrency of 72.5 mn streams (record); linear TV share 34.7%; digital entertainment watch time +35%. TV ad revenue under pressure from FMCG spend cuts.

segments.name: Oil to Chemicals (O2C)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA down 4% YoY; refinery throughput down 4% (FY26 19.5 vs 20.3 MMT). Gasoil crack averaged $35.4/bbl, ATF $36.3; gasoline crack $5.6. Downstream and polymer margins under pressure from elevated naphtha (up 13% YoY) and freight.

segments.name: Exploration & Production (KG-D6 / CBM)
segments.commentary: Production decline held to 8% vs 12-14% expected; Q4 EBITDA margin slightly lower on higher opex (asset integrity work, workovers). Gas price ceiling revised to about $8.9/MMBtu; CBM not subject to ceiling.

segments.name: New Energy
segments.commentary: Signed one of the world's largest green ammonia supply contracts with Samsung C&T. Targets 20 GW integrated solar/cell capacity and 100 GWh battery scaling; first 40 GWh BESS and cell phase commissioning in the year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects cracks to remain strong for some time given refinery damage in the Middle East and shipping/insurance concerns; structurally tight refining market.
Customs duty exemption on key petrochemicals valid to end of Q1 FY27; likely to be revoked in Q2 if prices moderate.
Jio IPO described as 'fairly imminent'; DRHP timing not given.
Retail square footage and store count expected to grow; no numeric guidance given.
Management expects Jio ARPU to rise 4-5% organically without tariff hikes; digital services to grow faster than connectivity from a smaller base.
Two large O2C projects (vinyl and PTA) prioritised for accelerated execution.
capex_capacity: Jamnagar green hydrogen/ammonia trains in detailed engineering and fabrication; Kutch 12 land parcels (5.3 lakh acres) under development; Kutch-Lakadia and Kutch-Jamnagar transmission EPC awarded.

Giga factories: module and cell lines commissioned with ALMM listing (first HJT lines in India); polysilicon, ingot, wafer, cell and glass commissioning targeted in next few quarters; integrated capacity 20 GW.
Battery scaling to 100 GWh with equipment orders placed; first 40 GWh BESS/cell phase commissioning during the year.
Gigawatt-scale AI data centres being worked on; progress updates expected in next few quarters.
E&P: rig for MGA field expected later this year; 40 multilateral CBM wells planned.
demand_pricing: Domestic fuel demand FY26: gasoline +6.5%, diesel +3.6%; Q4 domestic demand grew 2.7% YoY with gasoline +7%, diesel +5%, ATF +3%.
RBML (retail JV) volume growth ~27% YoY; 50-60 outlets added QoQ; CBG/CNG volumes +65%.
Naphtha price up 13% YoY; PE/PP demand +3%, PVC -10% (pipe-grade imports disrupted), polyester chain +16% on paraxylene strength.
Asian naphtha crackers ethylene operating rates fell from 80% to 60% during the disruption; Saudi OSP premium reportedly $20-30/bbl.
Retail LFL growth mid-to-high single digits; grocery and fashion posted double-digit growth; Ajio Luxe brand portfolio +24%; Jewels AOV +53%.
Jio: 5G users 54% of mobility consumers; monthly churn declining.

qa_highlights.question: How much could distillate yield change if refinery runs rely on alternate crudes (US, Africa, Venezuela) with different sulphur and gravity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the refinery is designed for heavy crudes and processes 200+ grades; Venezuelan re-entry is a positive, and Urals is a Middle East look-alike, so composition is not seen as a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How is the fuel retail business handling losses, and is there a price-increase trigger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail sales grew 20% or more YoY with ~4-5% market share; it will keep domestic supply without curtailment and take a long-term view, with PSUs bearing most of the under-recovery burden.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 outlook for crude premiums, freight and cracks?
qa_highlights.answer: Situation is fluid: cracks have cooled, and crude premiums that reached about $40/bbl are now around half that; management expects refining to stay structurally strong.

qa_highlights.question: Which products are affected by SAED?
qa_highlights.answer: Only diesel is materially affected in the domestic-focused DTA refinery output; jet is negligible, and the impact is a discount in the domestic channel.

qa_highlights.question: Retail growth decomposition: SSSG vs square footage vs quick commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RCPL demerger cut reported growth by ~3 pp; SSSG offline is healthy single digit; QC and B2B are ramping and pressuring margins. Declined to give a square footage growth number, only that it will grow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did JPL EBITDA rise faster than revenue, and when is the Jio IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin gain to operating leverage, as delivery costs did not rise with new contracts; IPO is 'fairly imminent' with no DRHP timing given. AI data centres sit in the intelligence entity, not JPL.

qa_highlights.question: What would success look like for Jio in terms of ROIC or FCF over 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give financial targets, citing priorities of mobility share, homes, enterprise and digital services scaling.

risks_watch: Crude supply and freight: refinery throughput fell to 19.5 MMT in FY26 from 20.3 MMT as Middle East supply was disrupted; management says cracks may stay strong but the situation is fluid.

Policy and regulatory exposure: SAED introduced effective 27 March 2026 hits domestic diesel; customs duty exemption on key petrochemicals runs to end Q1 FY27 and is likely to be revoked in Q2; fuel under-recoveries remain with retail.
Retail margin dilution: Q4 EBITDA margin at 7.9% as hyperlocal and quick commerce grow; management gave no timeline for margin stability and no square footage growth number.
Jio IPO timing: described as fairly imminent but no DRHP timing; earlier first-half 2026 expectation not confirmed on the call.
E&P decline and gas pricing: KG-D6 decline held at 8% but the gas ceiling price was revised to about $8.9/MMBtu, and the Qatar LNG outage affects Indian gas supply.
Petchem demand and feedstock: naphtha up 13% YoY, PVC demand down 10%, Asian cracker operating rates fell from 80% to 60%; vinyl and PTA mega-projects need timely execution.

So, the situation is very fluid. Nobody really knows what is going to happen.
It is fairly imminent. We are working towards it, and we will keep you posted.

500325|2026-06.headline: Reliance Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25% and EBITDA about 10% to over Rs 54,000 Cr, led by O2C spreads, with net profit near Rs 23,200 Cr (+6%).
500325|2026-06.overview: Consolidated topline rose about 25%, mainly on higher oil prices, with Jio revenue up 12% and retail up about 12% (underlying 11.6% ex-RCPL). Management backed out the Rs 8,900 Cr Asian Paints gain from the prior-year base, so EBITDA of over Rs 54,000 Cr is up 10% on a like-for-like basis. O2C revenue rose 17% to about Rs 17,000 Cr on distillate and chemical deltas, offset by SAED, under-recoveries, a planned turnaround and LPG and gas diversions. Net debt was slightly lower than March at about Rs 1,23,000 Cr, with capex of about Rs 39,000 Cr; Moody's upgraded RIL to Baa1 and S&P is at A-.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated EBITDA (recurring, ex Asian Paints gain)

financial_highlights.change: Pressured by higher net finance cost as 5G costs are now expensed
+12% YoY reported-basis adjusted for RCPL; +7.4% reported, +11.6% underlying
Slightly lower YoY; margin down 80 bps

segments.name: Oil to Chemicals (O2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs 17,000 Cr (+17%) on higher distillate and chemical deltas; refinery run near full capacity (~96-97% throughput) despite a planned turnaround that cut sale production ~10%. EBITDA margin fell YoY, with SAED, under-recoveries and higher crude differentials and freight as drags.

segments.name: Oil & Gas (E&P)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~3.2% YoY; EBITDA roughly flat. Condensate realisation about $107/bbl; KGD6 ceiling price $8.9/mmBtu, down ~$1.14, expected to rise by at least $1 in H2. CBM output crossed 1 mmscm/d.

segments.name: Jio Platforms
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 39,173 Cr (+11.8%), EBITDA Rs 20,865 Cr (+15.1%), margin 53.3%. 533.3 mn subscribers, 285 mn 5G users, 28.6 mn fixed broadband (14 mn AirFiber); ARPU Rs 215.6 (+Rs 7 YoY); digital services +20%.

segments.name: Reliance Retail
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs 90,000 Cr; EBITDA Rs 6,309 Cr, margin 7.9% (-80 bps). Digital commerce investment is depressing margins; orders +116% YoY in grocery, 1,000+ big box stores, and 4 mn B2B customers.

segments.name: JioStar
segments.commentary: Total revenue Rs 10,946 Cr (+14%); income from operations up ~30%. IPL 2026 was the biggest ever; 530 mn+ users; linear TV share 34%. Ad revenue was hit by the real-money gaming ad ban and the US-Iran conflict.

segments.name: Consumer / FMCG (RCPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 8,600 Cr, about 2x YoY; beverages Rs 2,900 Cr (>50% growth); daily essentials Rs 3,200 Cr. Management says EBITDA is breakeven; target Rs 1 lakh Cr revenue by FY2030.

segments.name: New Energy
segments.commentary: Solar PV: 1 GW peak of modules produced, targeting 20 GW annual by year end; battery target 40 GWh this year, scaled to 120 GWh. Kutch renewable power expected to flow this year; Samsung C&T green ammonia contract executed.

guidance_outlook: Retail: management targets doubling absolute EBITDA over about three years, with no margin target. Margins expected to dip short term as online scales.
Retail: FY27 is described as a foundation year; online growth is to be funded from existing profits.
KGD6 gas ceiling price expected to rise by at least $1/mmBtu in H2 FY27; rig due next month for KG Basin exploration.
Two additional ethane VLECs: first ship nearing US port loading, next two due in the coming months; ethane and ROGC expected to rise as a share of ethylene feed (currently ~70%).
Global demand expected to be lower in 2026 and rebound in 2027; refining cracks described as reasonably strong. Management declined to guide on the current-quarter run rate.
Jio: no specific guidance; management declined to give forward-looking statements on digital services margins or satellite investment.
FMCG: management expects growth to pick up in the next quarter in home care, personal care and processed food.
capex_capacity: Capex about Rs 39,000 Cr in Q1; management declined to give full-year capex, citing an EBITDA-to-debt and rating framework, and said partners may be evaluated.
Jamnagar 168 MW data centre for Meta, funded on RIL's balance sheet, to be delivered in one shot on a fast timeline (not disclosed).
Battery cell gigafactory ~40 GWh to be commissioned this year; solar cell lines commissioned and expanding; polysilicon construction nearing completion.
Kutch renewable ecosystem: installation to start after monsoon; power to flow once transmission is ready this year.
Partially commissioned large beverage plant (one of Asia's largest) and integrated food park in FMCG; a new edible oil facility is being explored in West Bengal.
Retail: dark store network to expand over the next 9-10 months; 1,000+ big box stores and ~2,221 retail outlets in fuel retail (about 230-240 added YoY).
demand_pricing: O2C: distillate margins up sharply (management said 250-300% on a flat crude basis, before crude differentials). Gasoline cracks $26/bbl (from $10), gasoil $63 (from $16), ATF $62 (from $14).
Brent averaged $104.5/bbl vs $68 in the prior-year period. Middle East OSP premiums reached ~$20/bbl, and freight rose ~10x.
Petrochemicals: polymer demand down 22%; polyethylene most affected, PVC least. Naphtha up 61% to $903/t (above $1,000 at peak).
Retail: transactions +46%, customers +11%, average transaction value falling as digital mix rises. Apparel digital share 27.5%.
Jio: ARPU Rs 215.6, up Rs 7 YoY with no tariff action; organic ARPU improvement cited at 4-5%; promotional offers in Homes business weigh on ARPU.
Gas: India gas consumption down ~10% YoY; PSC gas priority circular rolled back.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% digital services growth sustainable, and will its margin converge to connectivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward-looking guidance but said digital services growth is rising, with more monetisation potential. Margins are currently lower due to investment; they should improve as revenue scales.

qa_highlights.question: Why was ARPU up less than 1% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said underlying ARPU is not under pressure. Homes mix and promotional offers weigh on it; organic ARPU growth is 4-5% without tariff action.

qa_highlights.question: How will JioMart's quick commerce investment be measured, and what are its advantages?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Taluja said dark store expansion continues for about 9-10 months, with discipline on unit economics and no chasing of order volume. Advantages cited: 400 mn loyalty members, 20 years of data, presence in 1,000+ grocery markets, and better terms of trade.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a Jio order book or a process for platform services revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Anshuman Thakur gave a generic answer on vertical teams, targets and monitoring; no order book was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 168 MW Meta data centre be built on RIL's balance sheet, and what is the full-year capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The data centre is on RIL's own balance sheet with the group funding it, delivered in one shot on a clear timeline. Capex was not guided; the framework is EBITDA-to-debt and ratings, with partners possible.

qa_highlights.question: Current-quarter profitability and crude availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said crude is bought 45-50 days ahead and the outlook is uncertain. Ethane shortfall of 7-8% vs the 1.6 mt design should be closed with new VLECs; no run-rate guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: FMCG EBITDA and Independence revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Ketan Mody said FMCG is at EBITDA breakeven, improving with scale, and the Independence split will be shared later.

risks_watch: Crude availability and cost: Middle East supply disruption (Strait of Hormuz) persists; crude bought 45-50 days ahead, and management declined to say whether current-quarter profitability is better than Q1.

O2C earnings volatility: SAED, under-recoveries on domestic and PSU sales, LPG and gas diversions, and crude differentials/freight/OSP premiums can offset headline cracks; management said Q1 is not a steady-state number.

Retail margin pressure: EBITDA margin 7.9% (down 80 bps) as dark stores scale; target is to double absolute EBITDA over about three years with no margin target, and dark store expansion runs for the next 9-10 months.

Jio ARPU and digital services margins: ARPU up Rs 7 YoY but only slightly QoQ; Homes promotions weigh; digital services grow ~20% at lower margins than connectivity, and management declined forward guidance on margin convergence.

Gas and E&P: KGD6 natural decline; ceiling price $8.9/mmBtu expected to rise by at least $1 in H2; India gas consumption down ~10% YoY; PSC gas priority circular rolled back.

Execution milestones to track: 1 GW solar module output vs 20 GW annual target, 40 GWh battery cells this year, Kutch power flow this year, three ethane VLECs delivery, and FMCG Independence split to be shared later.

500325|2026-09.headline: Reliance Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA hit a record Rs 62,409 crore (+24% YoY) and PAT crossed Rs 50,000 crore on a half-year basis, led by O2C.
500325|2026-09.overview: Consolidated EBITDA rose 24% YoY to Rs 62,409 crore and PAT rose 34% to close to Rs 30,000 crore, both records for the company. O2C EBITDA rose 69% to Rs 25,203 crore on tight product markets, wide ethane-naphtha spreads and record crude runs, despite higher freight, insurance and crude premiums. Digital services EBITDA rose 18% to about Rs 22,200 crore, while Retail EBITDA fell about 10-11% to Rs 6,228 crore as it invests in online commerce. Management said the first-half run-rate points to annualised O2C EBITDA well above Rs 80,000 crore, though it cautioned that the earnings benefit is driven by geopolitical disruption.

segments.name: O2C (Oil to Chemicals)
segments.commentary: EBITDA Rs 25,203 crore, up 69% YoY, the strongest quarter seen. Gasoline cracks about 3x YoY, diesel about 3.5x, jet about 3.7x; ethane-naphtha differential at $557/t, up 2.3x YoY. Management expects FY27 O2C EBITDA of about Rs 80,000 crore.

segments.name: Jio Platforms
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 40,475 crore (+11.4% YoY), EBITDA Rs 21,879 crore (+16.6%), subscribers 542 million with 36 million net adds over 12 months, 300 million 5G users, 30 million homes connected; ARPU Rs 218.8 (+3.5% YoY without tariff hike). IPO listed at 26.7% premium, making it second-largest listed company by market cap.

segments.name: Reliance Retail
segments.commentary: Revenue +6.4% YoY, EBITDA Rs 6,228 crore (-11% YoY), margin 7.8%, down 140 bps YoY. Registered customers above 400 million (+10%); 303 stores opened and about 500 closed; online grocery revenue +42% YoY; ~20,000 stores, 77.5 million sq ft. Margin hit from online investment and price parity in quick commerce.

segments.name: Reliance Consumer Products (FMCG)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 8,266 crore (1.6x YoY); H1 Rs 16,900 crore (1.8x YoY). Entered ice cream via Bombay Creamery; presence expanded to Australia (Coles, Woolworths), Kenya and GCC/SE Asia markets.

segments.name: JioStar
segments.commentary: Total MAU on JioHotstar 440 million (+10% YoY); revenue +10% YoY, driven by D2C subscriptions and linear TV. Sports monetisation was weak early in the quarter due to Middle East overhang, improving by India-West Indies series; Drishyam 3 crossed Rs 500 crore global box office.

segments.name: Exploration and Production
segments.commentary: Production broadly flat QoQ; KG-D6 decline offset by higher gas prices and CBM uptrend. Gas ceiling price for the half raised by $1 to about $9.9/mmBtu. A deepwater rig returned to KG-D6 for workovers and development wells.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 O2C EBITDA of about Rs 80,000 crore, based on H1 tracking well above that annualised rate.
Retail: investment year in FY27; management says online economics improve from FY28 and benefits show in absolute EBITDA; target to double operating EBITDA in about two years is unchanged.

New energy: earnings contribution expected from FY28; module capacity 6+ GW now, targeting 20 GW early next year; solar cell about 5 GW now, targeting 20 GW in H1 CY27; BESS (40 GWh) commissioning next half, cell capacity (35-40 GWh) around late next year.
Jio capex tapering as 5G and UBR core network deployment completes; strong cash flow expected over the next several quarters.
Global oil demand projected to fall about 2.5-2.6 mb/d in 2026 and rebound 2-2.3 mb/d in 2027 (IEA), per management.
Three new ethane carriers: first operating, second on its way to US, third due shortly.
capex_capacity: Refinery utilisation at record crude runs despite Strait of Hormuz disruptions; coker, platformer and FCC running at high levels.
Ethane carrier fleet: one of three new vessels operating, second delivered and en route to US, third due shortly.
Data centre: 44 MW being completed over the next four to six months; plan for another 120 MW later; infra build for a hyperscaler customer.
Retail: 303 stores opened, about 500 unviable stores shut; retail area down about 1 million sq ft to 77.5 million sq ft; warehousing space flat.
Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio cited around 0.47 for September 2026; capex described as broadly flat QoQ.
demand_pricing: Brent ranged $70-130/bbl over the quarter; Q2 average $97 vs $69 pre-conflict. Physical crude premiums and freight rates elevated, raising OpEx.
Domestic fuel demand strong: MS +8.5% YoY, diesel +7.5% YoY, helped by deficient monsoon and under-recovery pricing.
Global polymer capacity impacted: PE, MEG and PTA together roughly 25-30% of global capacity affected; global cracker utilisation fell from 81% to 71%.
Naphtha availability from Middle East halved; naphtha AG-Japan freight rose from $86/t in July to $186/t in September.
Domestic polymer demand down 3% YoY on supply constraints; Jio ARPU up 3.5% YoY without tariff increase.
Jio fixed wireless holds over 78% share with 15.1 million connections.
Retail: online grocery share up 270 bps YoY; electronics distribution +20% YoY; premium phones strongly up; own brands up 710 bps share in apparel.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5 million barrels/day of refinery capacity still offline likely to normalise in 6-9 months, and what if it takes longer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed with the framing: remaining outages are in Russia (about 40% of capacity concerned) and Middle East refineries still ramping. No resolution is visible given ongoing attacks, so no near-term change is expected.

qa_highlights.question: How is crude sourcing being positioned given Middle East flows recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: Sourcing is switched month to month between East and West of Suez to chase the most advantageous crude; this approach continues into October-December.

qa_highlights.question: What drove O2C profit growth QoQ: refining, petchem or the new ethane carriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined effect. Petchem contributed, refining also; diesel up about $2.8/bbl QoQ; time-chartered fleet mitigated freight; gasifier benefited from high gas prices; product premiums also helped.

qa_highlights.question: Is the demand decline in China structural, and will refining margins fall below prior normal levels?
qa_highlights.answer: China's EV and LNG-truck shift is structural, but rest-of-world demand should more than offset it; management expects a strong 2027 rebound. It sees margins staying elevated because the market's memory of supply shocks will persist, not a normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Commissioning timelines for new energy lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Module capacity at 6+ GW rising to 20 GW early next year; solar cell about 5 GW rising to 20 GW in H1 CY27; BESS in the next calendar half and cell from June to December; transmission connectivity by Q1 next year; revenue expected in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Retail: when do investments taper and what is the margin trajectory? Plus data centre capex and IPL bid.
qa_highlights.answer: Competition remains intense; online margins structurally lower due to discounts and delivery costs; benefits expected from FY28 onwards. Data centre 44 MW in 4-6 months, 120 MW planned later. Management is keen to bid for IPL rights, with price discipline.

qa_highlights.question: Does a double-EBITDA target in two years still hold given weak online growth vs quick commerce peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail says the target is unchanged. Online growth is measured and funded from the existing 400 million customer base; economics should improve from next year.

qa_highlights.question: Has O2C spread capture improved, and will the two new vessels add further?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Petchem volumes improved as LPG control order relaxed; refining feedstock capture improved with regional switching; ethane advantage to grow with the incremental vessels.

500330|2026-03.headline: Raymond Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR85 crore (13.9% margin) from INR99 crore, while Engineering segments grew and a INR930 crore 5-year capex plan was announced.
500330|2026-03.overview: Consolidated total income rose 2% YoY to INR613 crore in Q4 FY26, but EBITDA fell to INR85 crore with a 13.9% margin versus INR99 crore and 16.4% a year earlier, as non-operating income dropped after INR600 crore was transferred to Raymond Realty post-demerger. For FY26, total income grew 10% to INR2,312 crore while EBITDA was flat at INR335 crore, with margin down to 14.5% from 15.9%. Aerospace & Defense revenue grew 26% for the year to INR392 crore, and Precision Technology & Auto Components grew 10% to INR1,667 crore with EBITDA up 34%, helped by synergies and a INR13 crore one-time land-sale gain. Management announced a INR930 crore five-year capex programme, including INR500 crore for Aerospace and INR430 crore for Precision Technology, with a new Andhra Pradesh aerospace plant targeted to start commercial production in the second half of calendar 2027.

Aerospace vane capacity: management says the current plant has enough capacity for doubled vane orders before the Andhra plant is used.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are adjusting to US tariffs; automotive tariffs are now 18%, while aerospace had no tariffs. Some delays and rescheduling were reported.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Precision Auto EBITDA margin expansion, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited SAP implementation in August, group integration, consolidated buying, cost reduction and efficiencies, and said margins should remain at current levels, with raw material pass-through lagging. The INR13 crore land-sale gain was excluded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and capex phasing for the Andhra plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial production in the second half or last quarter of FY28 (calendar 2027). Capex of about INR100 crore per business per year, so roughly INR200 crore a year across both.

qa_highlights.question: How much incremental aerospace revenue will Andhra add in FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers but said the first 25% growth year is met by the existing plant and the next comes from Andhra, which it framed as INR150-200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded given the INR68 crore net cash versus about INR1,000 crore borrowings in consolidated accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash includes liquid and some 2-3 year marketable investments. Management said the Engineering business is self-funding from cash flows, with the parent's liquidity as a backstop, and no parent capital infusion is planned for organic needs.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the aerospace business is LEAP engine exposure, and what is the customer concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not split the order book by programme, but said over 75% of products are for engines across OEMs and that it serves more than 25 customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation high relative to EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR800 crore of intangibles from the merger drive much of the depreciation, which is non-cash and gives a tax benefit, so cash generation is adequate.

500350|2026-03.headline: RSWM FY26 PAT turned positive at ₹52 crore (1.1% margin) from a ₹41 crore loss, while revenue fell 5.6% to ₹4,554 crore.
500350|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was ₹1,142 crore, up 4.5% QoQ but down 9.1% YoY, with exports at ₹368 crore (up 11.4% QoQ) and domestic sales at ₹774 crore. Q4 EBITDA was ₹85 crore at a 7.4% margin, up 115 bps YoY. For FY26, EBITDA rose 40.5% to ₹327 crore (7.1% margin, up 231 bps), helped by a ₹22.66 crore deferred tax liability write-back under the new tax regime. Management attributed the turnaround mainly to product-mix optimisation, exit from Chhata spinning (~₹250 crore revenue), working capital control and lower finance cost, and said it is not cyclical. Denim and knit were hit by gas disruption in March and by weak US/EU export demand, with utilisation expected to recover by 7-10 points.

Knit expansion of ₹92 crore: capacity from about 600 tons to 900 tons, including printing; full rollout targeted in Q3 FY27.
No other major capex planned beyond the knit expansion and plant modernisation; capex to focus on projects with 1-3 year payback.
Renewable energy: about 70% of energy mix now from wind and solar under the Adani round-the-clock tie-up.
Preferential issue of 24.7 lakh convertible warrants (about ₹36 crore) to LNJ Textile Advisory LLP, a promoter group entity, approved by the Board in April 2026.
demand_pricing: Global textile demand described as soft, with discretionary spending in Western markets cautious; the US tariff situation and the Gulf conflict disrupted trade flows and freight.
Price pass-through lags cost increases, especially in denim, where yarn, gas, dyes and freight have all risen; orders already booked cannot be repriced.
Yarn businesses are said to maintain spreads, with improvement in B2B yarn spreads.
Revenue decline came from the Chhata spinning exit (~₹250 crore) and weaker US-linked exports after the tariffs in Q3.
Management expects UK, EU and New Zealand FTAs to become operational around the end of 2026 or early 2027. The value-added share of sales is under one-fifth, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the recovery comes from product mix, discounts, energy, inventory discipline or exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the turnaround is internally driven, mainly product-mix optimisation and cutting low-contribution volumes, plus working-capital tightening (about ₹12.5 crore of interest savings). It did not give a percentage split.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US order book fully recovered after the tariff settlement?
qa_highlights.answer: Not fully. Management said it is under recovery; product development lost over three to six months is still affecting orders, and it expects about two more quarters to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Adani renewable power tie-up cut power costs, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated savings of about ₹1 per unit, around 3-4 lakh units per day (roughly ₹1 crore per month), varying by season with wind and solar output.

qa_highlights.question: What PAT impact came from the deferred tax reversal?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹23 crore. Management said PAT would have been ₹29 crore under the existing tax rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2B project funding structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Total cost ₹427 crore, about 70% project financing (₹300 crore loan approved), with the remainder from equity and holding-company loans (about ₹127 crore). The project was scaled down by 60-65% from the original ₹700-plus crore plan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said term loans are about ₹700 crore and working capital borrowings about ₹800 crore. Term loans are expected to reduce over the next three to four years.

segments.commentary: Revenue ₹232 cr, up 17% (volume +8%, price +9%). Exports ₹165 cr, up ~2.5%; CSM ₹27 cr vs ₹2 cr (PEKK rebound); Domestic B2B ₹39 cr, up 11%.

segments.name: Seeds
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹70 cr, down 31% on 26% volume decline; EBITDA nil and PAT ₹(4) cr vs ₹16 cr. Paddy and cotton placements fell on water shortage; management says seed inventory is elevated but fresh.

guidance_outlook: No numerical revenue or margin guidance given; management described the outlook as cautiously constructive and uneven recovery.
Expects next kharif season to be significantly better if monsoon normalises, though no forecast was given.
Capex: H2 FY27 to be higher than H1 (H1 under ₹20 cr); full-year capex about ₹50 cr, 'a little bit more than that'.
Expects to keep generating free cash flow for the full year as raw material purchases moderate and seed inventory normalises from March.
Seed production to slow in coming season; target to carry 150% of requirement in maize, rice and bajra.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex was below ₹20 cr; H2 to be higher to fund growth and sustenance projects.
New R&D centre in Navi Mumbai: consultants and government liaison complete, likely commissioning April 2027.
Overall capacity utilisation expected to remain broadly stable; growth via product mix and efficiencies.
Focus on capital efficiency across fixed and working capital; inventory elevated versus last year.
demand_pricing: Kharif 2026 hit by ~19% deficient rain in ~43% of India; slower liquidation and high carry-forward inventory.
Management says channel inventory is not elevated and products placed only where water availability is certain; kharif returns and provisions taken for most of the market.
Herbicide demand strong but price pressure; fungicide demand weak on low disease pressure and excess supply; insecticide and new launches grew well.
Cotton area shrank about 20-25% from peak (13 mn ha to 10-10.5 mn ha); illegal seed share estimated at 25-30%, now lower. Company says it gained share in North India cotton.
Export volumes hit by lower Pendimethalin AI demand in Europe, Chinese pricing, raw material constraints and 2-4 week supply chain delays; majority of exports to Americas.

qa_highlights.question: Are all kharif sales returns accounted for, and what is channel inventory like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said kharif returns are complete for most of the market, with provisions taken for the rest; channel inventory is only what is needed to close kharif and start rabi.

qa_highlights.question: Why did export B2B volumes decline in H1, and why did the low-cost raw material benefit not show in H1 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Export volume cuts were partly deliberate to protect margins; the low-cost inventory benefit was taken in Q1 and the weighted average benefit was lost in Q2 as prices were cut to compete.

qa_highlights.question: Why are fungicide prices not being passed on despite higher input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Low disease pressure cut demand while domestic supply and Chinese imports stayed high, so the planned price pass-through was withdrawn.

qa_highlights.question: What are the full-year capex and working capital expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex: H2 above H1, full year a little above ₹50 cr. Working capital expected to normalise from March as seed purchases fall; no red flags on receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 12-13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly freight and partly M&A-related fees for evaluated opportunities.

risks_watch: Weak rabi herbicide pricing in North India and continued fungicide price pressure.
Water availability for rabi and kharif 2027; subdued January-February rain forecast; reservoirs about 70% vs 76.6% 10-year average.
Export margins and volumes under freight, insurance and Red Sea routing pressure, plus China competition.
Elevated seed and raw material inventory and working capital; whether it normalises by year-end.
Cotton market: illegal seed share, acreage recovery, and government price cap on cotton seed.
Other expense growth (12-13%) and possible M&A-related fees.
500355|2026-09.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the quarter, attributing the weakness to rainfall and the geopolitical backdrop rather than strategy; management is confident in its portfolio and launches but gave no numerical forward guidance and was evasive on the precise sales breakup by state and seed crop.
key_quotes: Overall, EBITDA for Q2FY27 stood at ₹ 126 cr, lower by 18% compared to Q2 of the previous year.
Because of excessive supply. So as I said, our insecticide business did well.
So channel inventory, I think -- so first of all, we are not flooding the channel.
Now receivables, I think, at this point of time, we don't see any red flag. I think it's all under control.

500368|2026-03.headline: Patanjali Foods Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR11,156 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.48% and FY27 guidance points to 12-15% blended EBITDA growth.
500368|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue from operations at INR11,155.60 crore, with EBITDA excluding exceptional items of INR501.96 crore (4.48% margin) and PBT of INR235.69 crore (2.10% margin). FY26, the first full year after the HPC business integration, delivered revenue of INR40,169.58 crore, crossing the INR40,000 crore mark, with EBITDA of INR1,931.52 crore (4.79%). Edible oil and FMCG grew double digits, while staples (rice) and ghee softened sequentially in Q4. Management flagged a sharp crude-linked edible oil price spike from March 2026 and a further rise in April, which it expects to be beneficial to large players in the near term.

segments.name: Edible oil
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR8,324 crore (+23.28% YoY), EBITDA margin 2.58%; branded oil about 75% of edible oil sales. Edible oil volume 20.3 lakh tonnes vs 18.84 lakh tonnes last year; aggregate segment volume 25.1 lakh tonnes vs 23.64 lakh tonnes.

segments.name: FMCG (Foods + HPC)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR2,890 crore (25.76% of revenue) with 57.62% of EBITDA; FY26 revenue INR11,188 crore (+19.95%), EBITDA margin 10.81%.

segments.name: Biscuits
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR477.89 crore (+13.97% YoY), slightly down QoQ from INR490 crore in Q3; FY26 INR1,907.81 crore (+15.9%), highest ever. Doodh biscuits FY26 turnover over INR1,300 crore vs INR1,000 crore in FY25. Q4 EBITDA INR65 crore.

segments.name: Staples and ghee
segments.commentary: Staples Q4 revenue INR848.83 crore, FY26 INR3,658 crore; sequential drop of about INR407 crore driven mainly by rice. Ghee Q4 INR338.91 crore, FY26 INR1,423.86 crore; ghee sales fell about INR129 crore on early-summer and Middle East disruption. Staples Q4 EBITDA INR5.46 crore.

segments.name: Ethnic foods (Foods business)
segments.commentary: Foods business Q4 EBITDA INR72 crore combined, of which ethnic foods INR66 crore and staples INR5.46 crore. Mid-teens YoY decline was flagged by an analyst; management did not dispute the figure.

segments.name: Nutrela (soya/textured)
segments.commentary: Nutrela Q4 revenue INR106 crore, FY26 INR527 crore; Q4 EBITDA INR16.85 crore. Textured soya FY26 revenue INR526.78 crore.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR17.94 crore, FY26 INR58 crore after portfolio rationalisation; Q4 EBITDA INR2 crore.

segments.name: Home and Personal Care (HPC)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR840.50 crore (+35.42% YoY), EBITDA INR136 crore. Dental INR425.97 crore in Q4 and INR1,412.80 crore in FY26; skin care INR239.75 crore in Q4 (+57.66% YoY), FY26 INR680 crore; home care INR97.82 crore in Q4, FY26 INR331.88 crore.

segments.name: Oil palm plantation
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,793 crore and EBITDA INR357 crore vs INR203 crore prior year, helped by maturing plantations and higher palm oil prices. Cultivated area 1,10,722 hectares as of 31 March 2026, +23.65% YoY; about 38% in the 7-25 year prime yielding phase.

guidance_outlook: Edible oil volume growth of about 3-5% in FY27, in line with expected national consumption growth; management said it is slightly below 4%.
Foods portfolio revenue growth of 8-10% on a blended basis in FY27, with Foods margins expected to recover to about 10% after FY26 softness.
HPC revenue growth target of about 15% in FY27, with EBITDA margin near or above 18%, about 200 bps better than under the parent.
Blended EBITDA growth of 12-15% expected in FY27.
Edible oil EBITDA maintained in a 2-4% range despite near-term price volatility.
Q1 and Q2 FY27 expected to be very positive for edible oil and oilseed crushing, given Indonesian export-centralisation disruption.
Biscuit target of high double-digit growth, with Q1 FY27 expected to show a substantial uptick from INR478 crore in Q4 FY26.
capex_capacity: Oil palm cultivated area 1,10,722 hectares at 31 March 2026, +23.65% YoY and +2,558 hectares QoQ; total allocated area 6.63 lakh hectares.
Oil palm production fell in Q4 FY26 due to seasonality, while maturing plantations are expected to drive volume growth.
No new capex or commissioning timelines were given in the call.
demand_pricing: Palm, soyabean and sunflower oil prices rose about 20%, 23% and 22% respectively between January and March 2026 (RBD palm, refined soy and sunflower, per prepared remarks); April 2026 YoY increases were palm 15%, soybean 17%, sunflower 22%.
Consumer shift toward mustard oil observed as palm-linked prices rose; mustard, groundnut and cottonseed are domestic oils.
Edible oil price hikes were passed through almost daily; management said prices rose 10-15% (about 14% overall) and that its prices moved in line with the market.
Staples and ghee price hikes of 2-5% taken; ethnic foods other than ghee largely not repriced. Pulses and rice also repriced.
Cost of goods sold rose 98 bps QoQ and 294 bps YoY in Q4 FY26, with pressure from packaging, freight and insurance after mid-March.
Receivable days rose; INR700-800 crore of extra credit extended to customers. Advances paid to vendors for raw material security raised borrowings.
Rice category demand declined substantially through FY26; drought/El Nino and government policy risks flagged for staples.
Retail inflation 3.4% in March 2026 vs 3.21% in February 2026.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever quarterly revenue; YoY change not stated
Low tax charge: tax netted against refunds of INR788 crore in FY26, including INR330 crore in Q4
Crossed INR40,000 crore; double-digit growth in edible oil and FMCG

financial_highlights.value: INR2,890 crore, EBITDA INR292.16 crore, 10.11% margin

financial_highlights.metric: Oil palm plantation revenue / EBITDA (Q4 FY26)
financial_highlights.value: INR1,793 crore revenue, INR357 crore EBITDA
financial_highlights.change: EBITDA vs INR203 crore in prior-year period (as stated on call)
Oil palm segment revenue of INR185 crore in Q4 cited in prepared remarks

qa_highlights.question: Biscuit category growth in Q4 FY26, whether it met expectations, and how the category is shaping up in April-May.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said biscuit growth was roughly 13% YoY (initially said over 15%, later corrected) and a marginal sequential dip from INR490 crore in Q3 to INR478 crore in Q4, attributed to seasonality and consumption disruption. Target remains high double-digit growth; Q1 FY27 expected to show a substantial uptick from INR478 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Foods revenue fall mid-teens YoY in Q4, and was there a one-off in the low tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Rice demand fell substantially through FY26, and ghee sales dropped about INR129 crore on early summer onset and Middle East disruption. Q4 tax was low because the company netted earlier-year refunds of INR788 crore in FY26, including INR330 crore in Q4, against current tax demand following post-CIRP assessment.

qa_highlights.question: Segment EBITDA for the quarter (Foods, biscuits, nutraceuticals, Nutrela, HPC).
qa_highlights.answer: Foods combined EBITDA INR72 crore (ethnic foods INR66 crore, staples INR5.46 crore); biscuits INR65 crore; nutraceuticals INR2 crore; Nutrela INR16.85 crore; HPC INR136 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Edible oil volumes for Q4 and FY26, and price hikes taken.
qa_highlights.answer: Edible oil volume 20.3 lakh tonnes vs 18.84 lakh tonnes; aggregate segment volume 25.1 lakh vs 23.64 lakh tonnes. Edible oil volume rose about 80,000 tonnes Q3 to Q4 and 1.5 lakh tonnes over FY25 to FY26. Oil price increases of 10-15% (about 14%) were passed through almost daily; staples up 2-5%, ghee repriced, other ethnic foods largely not repriced.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and higher borrowings: what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Extra customer credit of about INR700-800 crore was extended amid market conditions, and advances were paid to vendors to secure raw materials, raising borrowings. Management aims to collect receivables within one to two quarters and return to cash procurement if geopolitics permit.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 guidance for edible oil volume, Foods and HPC revenue and margins, and blended EBITDA.
qa_highlights.answer: Edible oil volume growth 3-5%, slightly below 4%. Foods revenue growth 8-10% blended, with Foods margin recovering to about 10%. HPC revenue growth about 15% with EBITDA margin 18%-plus, about 200 bps better than under the parent. Blended EBITDA growth 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Near-term impact of Indonesian palm oil export centralisation on edible oil revenue and margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the disruption to private trade creates short-term volatility but benefits large players holding inventory; Q1 and Q2 FY27 expected to be very positive for edible oil and oilseed crushing. Volume growth still tracks national consumption of about 3-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Palm oil plantation EBITDA for Q4 and FY26.
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 plantation revenue INR1,793 crore and EBITDA INR357 crore, vs INR203 crore prior year (a prior-year figure of INR1,262 crore was also cited, apparently a revenue number). Drivers: maturing plantations and higher palm oil prices.

risks_watch: Crude-linked edible oil price volatility and Indonesian export centralisation; management expects Q1-Q2 FY27 to benefit but the pass-through pattern and margin outcome are unproven.
Edible oil EBITDA margin of 2.58% in Q4 and FY26 against a 2-4% target range; consumer shift toward mustard oil could affect branded mix.
Foods weakness: rice demand decline, drought/El Nino and government policy risk for staples; ghee softness linked to Middle East disruption.
Working capital stress: receivable days up with INR700-800 crore extra credit to customers and higher borrowings from vendor advances; collection timeline is one to two quarters.
Biscuit growth slowed to about 13% YoY from over 15% in Q3 (per management correction); watch whether Q1 FY27 shows the promised uptick.
Low Q4 tax charge due to refunds of INR788 crore; PBT margin of 2.10% in Q4 means reported profit quality depends on one-time refund adjustments.
key_quotes: So, the overall market growth, I think we should be quite aligned to that.
I think we should see a good growth of anywhere between 12% to 15% growth for the next year.
But overall, the target that we continue to place for ourselves is upwards in high double digits.
Crude-linked volatility remains elevated, which would make the operating environment increasingly challenging for smaller and unorganized players.

500368|2026-06.headline: Patanjali Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to INR11,337 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR543 crore (4.80% margin).
500368|2026-06.overview: Management reported the fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue, led by edible oils (INR8,505 crore, record) and oil palm (INR740 crore, up 25% YoY). FMCG revenue was INR2,938 crore at a 6.45% EBITDA margin, with biscuits and HPC growing strongly while staples were loss-making at INR-59 crore EBITDA. Input inflation from delayed monsoon and West Asia conflict was a net positive for edible oils (long positions) but a headwind for FMCG. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, while flagging caution on staples demand and margins.

segments.name: Edible oil
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8,505 crore, record, led by mustard oil; EBITDA margin 5.22%. Veg oil inflation helped as the company is long edible oils.

segments.name: Oil palm plantation
segments.commentary: Revenue INR740 crore, up 25% YoY. Cultivated area 1,15,861 ha as of 30 June 2026 against 6.63 lakh ha allocated; about 37% in the 7-25 year prime yielding phase.

segments.name: Biscuits
segments.commentary: Revenue INR560 crore, up 27% YoY, EBITDA margin 15.35% vs 9.35%. Doodh Biscuit (INR5 and INR10 packs) is cited at about INR1,300 crore annual business.

segments.name: Textured soya (Nutrela)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR160 crore, up 14% YoY and 50% QoQ, EBITDA margin above 18%. Management cites about 40% market share.

segments.name: Ghee
segments.commentary: Revenue INR219 crore, softer on seasonal demand and lower Middle East off-take amid geopolitical disruption.

segments.name: Beverages
segments.commentary: Revenue INR38 crore, helped by extended summer and launches of mango chutney, mango panna juice and orange juice.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR18 crore; management says the segment has turned EBITDA-positive from earlier marginal losses, with sports nutrition gaining momentum.

segments.name: Home & Personal Care
segments.commentary: Revenue INR629 crore: dental INR325 crore, skin care INR165 crore, home care INR83 crore, hair care and others INR56 crore. Skin care was the main growth driver.

segments.name: Staples and ethnic foods
segments.commentary: Staples revenue above INR1,000 crore with EBITDA of INR-59 crore; ethnic foods (honey, dry fruits, spices, herbal etc.) revenue INR203 crore with EBITDA INR9 crore.

guidance_outlook: Full-year edible oil volume growth of 3% to 5%, with edible oil margin construct of 3% to 5% (also cited as 2% to 4% later in the call).
Food and FMCG growth of 8% to 10%; beauty and personal care growing around 15%.
FMCG vertical EBITDA growth of 12% to 15% for the year; later described as 10% to 12% EBITDA growth overall.
Textured soya margin guided at 16% to 18%, with management expecting to stay above 18%.
FMCG revenue expected to reach about INR12,500 crore this year from about INR11,000 crore+ last year (CEO estimate).
Oil palm business expected to grow more than 15% this year.
Management aims for EBITDA of about INR2,500 crore over the next 18 months on an annualised basis (CEO view, not formal guidance).
E-commerce and quick commerce plus modern trade targeted to rise from about 15% to 20% of revenue within 18 months.
capex_capacity: Oil palm cultivated area 1,15,861 ha as of 30 June 2026 out of 6.63 lakh ha allocated under the National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm.
No capex or new capacity figures were discussed on the call.
demand_pricing: Foods volume grew about 5% YoY and pricing about 12% (management corrected an earlier approximation of 7-8% volume growth).
Calibrated price increases taken in edible oils; targeted discounts in FMCG; smaller pack sizes introduced. Pricing measures continue in Q2.
Palm oil prices firmed from March 2026, eased late in the quarter, then recovered to a two-week high in mid-August; rupee depreciated about 2.5%.
Soya oil futures rose about 40% by end-March, then stabilised; FOB prices corrected 6%.
Milk and sugar prices firmed; wheat stable. Packaging, freight and logistics costs rose in the quarter.
Management cautious on staples: El Nino food inflation uncertainty and rural demand stress; staples expected to see the most rural pressure in Q2.
Dishwash: management says no plans to exit or slow down, with variant launches continuing as the MNC exits.

financial_highlights.value: INR2,938 crore; EBITDA INR190 crore; margin 6.45%
financial_highlights.change: About 26% of revenue and about 30% of EBITDA excl. unallocable income

financial_highlights.value: INR629 crore revenue; EBITDA INR122 crore

qa_highlights.question: Given a large MNC temporarily exiting dishwash and Godrej Consumer reportedly exiting liquid dishwash, is there a big opportunity for Patanjali in the segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no intention to exit or slow down dishwash, variants will keep launching, and the market is expanding. It did not have the dishwash-specific number to hand and offered to share it after the call.

qa_highlights.question: With competitors' odd-price biscuits (INR4.5, INR9) now largely gone, how does this affect growth for the market leader and Patanjali?
qa_highlights.answer: Doodh Biscuit (INR5 and INR10 packs) is cited at almost INR1,300 crore annual business. Biscuit EBITDA margin was nearly 15% in the quarter, with management committed to INR5 and INR10 price points and adding premium variants such as Almond and Chyawanprash cookies.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management more cautious on staples than peers, and what price hikes were taken by category?
qa_highlights.answer: Caution rests on El Nino food inflation uncertainty and rural income and demand stress, plus pending policy on commodity control orders. Management stayed positive on top-line growth and reaffirmed staples/food growth of 8% to 10%; it did not give category-wise price hike details in this answer.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the foods recovery across ethnic foods and staples?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to inflation-driven buoyancy, sequential staples revenue growth of about INR260 crore (about 30%), and focus on niche items like Kesar and rice, plus new lentil and besan variants. Ethnic foods had seen some contraction, and margins are lower in this business.

qa_highlights.question: What were the volume and pricing split for foods, and the EBITDA for ethnic foods, HPC and staples?
qa_highlights.answer: Foods volume grew about 5% YoY and pricing about 12%, correcting an earlier 7-8% volume estimate. EBITDA was INR9 crore for ethnic foods, INR122 crore for HPC, and negative INR59 crore for staples.

qa_highlights.question: Is TSP (Nutrela) margin resilient when soya and food inflation rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged TSP typically does less well in high commodity inflation because pass-through is limited, and the space is hyper-competitive. It still reaffirmed a 16% to 18% margin for the year, with Q1 above 18% on INR160 crore revenue and about 40% market share.

qa_highlights.question: What are the structural drivers beyond FY27, and what is the target EBITDA path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited oil palm growth of more than 15% this year, margin expansion in HPC, Nutrela and biscuits, and edible oil margins moving from 2-4% toward 5%-plus. It cited a CEO view of moving toward about INR2,500 crore EBITDA over the next 18 months on an annualised basis.

qa_highlights.question: Did the acquisition of the HPC business from Patanjali Ayurved (INR1,100 crore) get overpaid, and what is the valuation basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business was acquired on a slump sale basis in November 2024 with no valuation methodology, that it generated about INR600 crore EBITDA last year on INR2,900 crore revenue, and that the price was recovered in under 18-19 months. The CFO said the details were disclosed to the exchanges and approved by shareholders.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q1 profit growth (84% YoY, as cited by the analyst) be sustained for Q2 to Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to extrapolate Q1 and pointed to staying within guidance: growth of 10%-plus YoY, foods 8%-10%, HPC 15%, and edible oil 2%-4%, with EBITDA growth of 10%-12%.

risks_watch: Staples profitability: segment EBITDA of INR-59 crore, with management flagging El Nino food inflation, rural demand stress, and pending policy on commodity control orders for Q2.
Edible oil margin construct: management gave differing ranges (3-5% and 2-4%) for the year, and the edible oil gain depends on continued veg oil inflation and palm and soya price moves.
TSP margin guidance of 16-18% is exposed to soya price spikes and rising competition, since pass-through is limited.
Related-party HPC acquisition (INR1,100 crore, slump sale): the analyst raised valuation concerns and a share price fall, and the company declined to provide further clarification on the call.
Pending legal matter (Ashav Advisory, sub judice) and management's refusal to discuss details on the call.

500378|2026-03.headline: Jindal Saw Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA fell to INR413 crore and PAT to INR114 crore, with export shipments suspended since March 2026 due to MENA conflict.
500378|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 weakened versus Q3 on both standalone and consolidated bases, missing management's prior guidance that Q4 would beat Q3. Standalone EBITDA was INR413 crore (Q3: INR527 crore) and PAT was INR114 crore (Q3: INR227 crore), while FY26 standalone EBITDA fell 47% and PAT fell 58% year on year. Management attributed the drop to weak ductile iron pipe demand from slow Jal Jeevan Mission execution, suspended exports from March 1, 2026 after MENA force majeure, a INR48 crore forex loss, and an API monogram suspension on seamless pipes. Net debt declined, with standalone net debt at INR2,453 crore. Management guided that Q1 FY27 will also be affected.

500378|2026-06.headline: Jindal Saw Q1 FY27 standalone PAT fell about 70% YoY to INR110 crores on MENA export shutdown, JJM delays and seamless API suspension.
500378|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose about 13% YoY to INR3,756 crores, but EBITDA fell about 40% to INR341 crores and PAT fell about 70% to INR110 crores. Outward shipments to MENA have been suspended since March 2026 due to the Strait of Hormuz blockade, and the seamless API licence was suspended from January to mid-June 2026. Management guided H1 to be softer, with H2 expected to improve, and said FY27 volumes should be flat with FY26. Abu Dhabi seamless (USD300 million, 3 lakh tons) and Saudi LSAW/HSAW JV projects are progressing, with commercial operations targeted for FY29.

segments.commentary: Delivered about 34,000 MT in Q1 FY27 vs 48,000 MT in Q4 FY26, with sales restricted to in-range trucking customers. Order book is about USD188 million, or 1.77 lakh tons, giving 3-4 quarters of visibility.

segments.name: Jindal Hunting (51% JV with Hunting Energy Services)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR5 crores with a first-ever loss of INR5.3 crores in Q1, attributed to the API licence suspension.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volumes are expected to be broadly flat versus FY26, provided the current situation persists.
H1 FY27 is expected to be softer; management expects H2 to improve over H1, though it does not usually give forward numbers.
Middle East dispatches are expected to stay at about 10,000-12,000 tons per month, road-only, until the sea route reopens.
Seamless Nashik utilisation is expected to ramp from about September-October, reaching roughly 70,000-80,000 tons per quarter.
Abu Dhabi seamless plant (3 lakh tons, about USD300 million) targets commercial operation in FY29, with financial closure expected in the next few months.
Post-project term debt is estimated at about INR3,500 crores, excluding working capital, versus about INR500 crores of long-term debt now.
No domestic capacity additions are planned beyond the Middle East projects.

Long-lead equipment is being procured through LCs and cash advances, and leasehold land with existing civil infrastructure has been secured. Commissioning is expected in roughly 18-20 months, with 50-60% utilisation in year one.

Saudi JV (51% Jindal Saw, 49% Buhur): LSAW and HSAW mills of 300,000 MT per annum each. Land is secured and LCs are opened for selected equipment. Interim financial closure is expected within a few months, with execution in about 1.5 years.
Abu Dhabi DI pipe facility is 1 lakh tons. Management assumes about 50% utilisation across the new facilities, with peak utilisation in FY30-31.

Nashik seamless API licence was reinstated in mid-June 2026, and participation in API tenders has restarted. Utilisation is expected to dip for about a quarter before improving from September-October.
Capacity utilisation was about 60-65% in FY26 and is similar in the current period.
demand_pricing: Order book is about 1.78 million tons, of which about 0.75 million tons is export. Export order book is about 60% Middle East and 40% non-Middle East.
Export order split by product: about USD70 million LSAW, USD30 million seamless and USD40 million DI, excluding the 6.08 lakh ton Saudi helical SAW job-work order.
Exports to MENA have been suspended since March 2026. Management is exploring job-work options for the Saudi order and is engaging buyers on alternative routes.
Domestic JJM-linked water demand remains weak due to delayed central funds and title scrutiny. Some uptick was seen in state-driven projects and in DI volumes in Q1.
The company is diversifying exports to Europe (existing presence in Italy), Latin America, Southeast Asia and CIS. Historically the mix was about 30% export and 70% domestic.
Hydrogen-transport pipe qualification (API 5L 70,000 psi, Italy lab) is complete, but management has not yet seen significant ground-level demand.

qa_highlights.question: How should one view FY27 execution, and when will volumes recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Goyal said FY27 volumes are expected to match FY26 if the current situation holds. Middle East dispatches are fixed at about 10,000-12,000 tons per month by road until the sea route reopens.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said interest is mainly on working capital and term loans, about INR70-75 crores per quarter. Q4 FY26 was hit by rupee depreciation, while Q1 was stable, and this run-rate is expected to continue if the rupee is stable.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines and utilisation for the MENA projects?
qa_highlights.answer: The LSAW/HSAW plants can be done in 18-24 months and the seamless plant in 18-20 months. Management assumes about 50% utilisation and peak utilisation in 2-3 years from FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nashik seamless run-rate outlook after the API reinstatement?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation should dip for about a quarter and improve from September-October. Quarterly volumes are expected to be about 70,000-80,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin pressure bottoming, and will H2 improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are under pressure from low utilisation and fixed-cost absorption. Management expects H2 to improve over H1, though Q2 may look similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What peak term debt is expected after the projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Term debt is about INR500-plus crores now and is estimated at about INR3,500 crores once the projects are complete. Working capital is additional.

financial_highlights.change: +11% from INR3,814 crore; EBITDA/ton INR1,161 vs INR1,071

financial_highlights.value: INR6,400 crore net cash; ~INR1,500 crore borrowings; gross ~INR7,900 crore

segments.name: India cement (standalone + Shree Cement East)
segments.commentary: Q4 capacity utilisation 66% (North 70%, East 60%, South 61%) vs 56% in Dec 2025. Installed capacity reached 69.3 Mt after Kodla (Karnataka) integrated project of 3.65 Mt clinker and 3.5 Mt cement commissioned in the quarter.

segments.name: Union Cement (UAE)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 45.65 lakh tons (+18%) and revenue AED 870 million (+39%). Sales slowed over the last two months due to Middle East tension; management expects recovery once peace returns. A 2.5 Mt cement mill is scheduled for September 2026.

segments.name: RMC business
segments.commentary: 26 plants operational at end-FY26; 10 more inaugurated in March 2026 and under commissioning, taking the count to 36. Q4 RMC revenue INR90 crore on 1.99 lakh m3; FY26 revenue INR246 crore. Management says it is too early to report RMC separately.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cement volume guided at about 40 Mt (management clarified this includes at most 0.2-0.3 Mt of clinker), versus 36.4 Mt in FY26.
FY27 capex estimated at about INR1,500 crore, covering RMC plants (target 50-55), railway sidings and preliminary Meghalaya work; the 80 Mt by FY29 target is retained but described as dynamic.
Depreciation guidance of INR1,600-1,700 crore for FY27 reaffirmed.

Fuel cost per kcal (landed) at INR1.60 in Q4 expected to rise 10-12% in Q1 FY27 to INR1.76-1.80; packing cost up about INR20/ton in Q4 with a further ~INR80-100/ton expected; management guided total cost impact of INR150-200/ton for Q1 FY27 vs March 2026. Q2 not commented on.
Price hikes of about INR25/bag taken in the past month, which management says covers anticipated cost increases up to June.
Management will move to consolidated reporting from next quarter.
capex_capacity: Kodla, Karnataka integrated project (3.65 Mt clinker, 3.5 Mt cement) commissioned in Q4 FY26; India installed capacity now 69.3 Mt.
Union Cement UAE 2.5 Mt cement mill scheduled for commissioning by September 2026.

Meghalaya integrated plant: 0.95 Mt clinker and 0.99 Mt cement; first block holds ~600 Mt limestone; ultimate capacity 4-4.5 Mt; capex about INR1,800 crore due to front-ended infrastructure. Mines are allocated by the state, not auctioned; no incentives confirmed yet.
Green power capacity 666.5 MW; green electricity 61% of consumption in Q4 FY26 (59% in Q4 FY25). Clinker factor 64.8% in Q4 (63.9% in Dec 2025).
Mauritius wholly owned subsidiary incorporated for cement, blending, storage and packing facilities.
demand_pricing: Management says the company has moved to a more stable pricing platform, narrowing the gap with the top player by INR15-20/bag, and is now pursuing volume share.
Q4 fuel mix: pet coke 54%, coal 32%, alternative fuel 14%. Trade sales 64% and blended cement 62% of volume (as stated in call).
Lead distance rose by about 12 km QoQ to 457 km in Q4, driving freight cost up roughly INR80/ton YoY and QoQ; target is below 440 km.
Management expects industry demand at 7.1-7.2% growth on 6.5% GDP assumption, with the company growing 1% above industry average.
Demand was healthy until 15 April 2026; slowdown since then, linked to Middle East conflict and moderate monsoon forecast.
Premium products share rose to 22% from 15% (about 9% two years ago).

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and cash deployment given cash surplus near INR9,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR1,500 crore (RMC, railway sidings, Meghalaya). Net cash INR6,400 crore and gross borrowings ~INR1,500 crore. Company has not borrowed for capex in about 15 years; plans to continue funding from internal accruals and may front-end capex if conditions improve.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 volume run rate match Q4's 11% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is about 40 Mt for FY27, including at most 0.2-0.3 Mt clinker; company targets 1% above industry growth, which management expects at 7.1-7.2%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost inflation outlook and how much is passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel cost per kcal to rise 10-12% in Q1 (INR1.60 to ~INR1.76-1.80). Packing cost up ~INR20/ton in Q4 and ~INR80-100/ton more ahead. Total Q1 cost impact INR150-200/ton. Price hikes of ~INR25/bag taken; management says these cover costs up to June, with Q2 not commented on.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 80 Mt by FY29 target still valid given utilisation in the low 60s?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 80 Mt by 2029 is still on record but capex has slowed and the situation is dynamic; too early to say if it will slip.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company protect EBITDA/ton while chasing volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says profitability is the prime focus and it will not enter a price war; it has never given EBITDA/ton or price guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to cut costs (WHRS, RE, clinker factor, railway)?
qa_highlights.answer: All kilns have or will have WHRS; RE target not given (to be shared next call); BESS being explored; railway doubling being pursued at three to four sites without numbers; clinker factor said to be among the best in the industry.

risks_watch: Fuel and packing cost inflation: fuel 10-12% higher in Q1 and packing costs rising (PVC granules); management gave no Q2 view and cost pass-through depends on demand.
Demand slowdown since mid-April 2026 linked to Middle East conflict, steel and labour cost pressure, and a moderate monsoon forecast.
Lead distance (457 km in Q4) and freight cost pressure; management targets below 440 km.
Competitive pressure risk in the North as capacity is added, as flagged by a peer's chairman; management did not rule out share loss.
Meghalaya incentives not yet confirmed by the state government; project capex of INR1,800 crore.
Union Cement (UAE) sales slowed over the last two months; recovery depends on Middle East ceasefire holding.
500387|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and on pricing discipline, but noticeably evasive on Q2 FY27 costs, EBITDA/ton and North market share. Management repeatedly declined to quantify forward cost impact or give specific targets, saying the situation is dynamic.
key_quotes: We have delivered on both these accounts, which explains our ethos of delivery and not proclamation.
We have never in our history given any guidance on EBITDA per ton.
Profitability is the prime focus. Price always the market gives. Volume is what we are capable to produce.
Maybe next quarter onwards, we will talk of consol only.
