500440|2026-06.headline: Hindalco Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 58% YoY to INR13,481 crore and PAT 75% to INR7,013 crore, led by record India upstream EBITDA of INR7,390 crore.
500440|2026-06.overview: Consolidated business segment EBITDA rose 58% YoY to INR13,481 crore and PAT rose 75% to INR7,013 crore, with Hindalco India EBITDA up 73% to INR8,606 crore. India upstream aluminium posted a record INR7,390 crore EBITDA (USD2,331/t, 55% margin) on higher LME and favourable macros, while copper delivered a record INR918 crore despite a planned smelter shutdown. Novelis volumes fell 5% YoY to 916 kt and adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to USD516 million, but the Oswego fire outage and elevated US tariffs (USD70 million) weighed on the quarter. Management guided volumes higher in Q2 for downstream aluminium and copper, and said sulphuric acid prices will stay near Q1 levels in Q2.

segments.name: India upstream aluminium
segments.commentary: Shipments up 3% YoY and revenue up 44% YoY; record EBITDA of INR7,390 crore. Hedged about 29% of FY27 aluminium at USD3,004/t and 18% of FX at INR91.63/USD.

segments.name: India downstream aluminium
segments.commentary: Shipments up 3% YoY to 104 kt; EBITDA INR298 crore, up 30%, on volume, mix and premiumisation. Management sees a sustainable downstream margin nearer USD250/t than the USD300 seen in Q1.

segments.name: India copper
segments.commentary: Metal shipments 105 kt, down 16% YoY on a planned smelter shutdown; CCR volumes 96 kt, down 8%. Record EBITDA of INR918 crore; ex-shutdown EBITDA/t would have been around USD1,000.

segments.name: Novelis
segments.commentary: Shipments 916 kt, down 5% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA USD516 million including an $18 million net positive from Oswego fires and $47 million insurance proceeds. Cost savings run-rate at USD225 million against a USD350-400 million target by FY28 exit; Oswego mill restarted in June.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 sulphuric acid prices expected to stay near Q1 levels; management hopes for no tapering in H2.
Q2 volumes expected higher for both India copper and India downstream aluminium.
India cash cost expected to rise 5-6% QoQ in Q2 on northern-region coal prices during monsoon.
Novelis net leverage expected to fall below 4x, with a level of about 4.5x around end-September; Novelis net debt/EBITDA to start declining in Q4.
Novelis working capital release of USD300-400 million over the next couple of quarters.
Novelis long-term EBITDA/t guidance of USD600 unchanged; Oswego net cash impact seen at about USD600 million after all insurance recoveries.
Consolidated net leverage to remain around 2x; India net debt/EBITDA not expected to change materially as FY27 is a high-capex year.
Aditya refinery and first 180 kt smelter phase commissioning Dec 2027; second phase Dec 2028; meaningful contribution in FY29. Captive coal: Chakla about 1 Mt and Bandha about 0.5 Mt in FY28.
capex_capacity: Aditya alumina refinery and aluminium smelter expansions progressing on track; strategy to double upstream capacity.
Captive coal mines: Chakla, Bandha and Meenakshi under development. Chakla about 1 Mt and Bandha about 0.5 Mt expected in FY28.
Renewables: 470 MW operational; 414 MW solar/wind and 90 MW RE-RTC pumped storage to be added in FY27, taking the portfolio to 884 MW solar/wind/hydel and 125 MW RE-RTC.
Novelis Bay Minette 600 kt greenfield rolling and recycling plant on track for completion in 2026, with initial commissioning underway.
Aditya Battery Foil and Taloja AC Fins commissioned last quarter and in customer qualification; specialty alumina (precipitated hydrate) nearing commercialisation.
Copper smelter expansion, Pakhajan scrap melting project (commissioning this year, IRR in high teens) and copper smelter timing under review, with smelter output expected in FY29.
demand_pricing: LME aluminium moved from about INR3,150/t before the Middle East conflict to a peak near USD3,850/t, then eased to USD3,200/t after the ceasefire; management expects a 2026 deficit of about 1 Mt.
India aluminium demand about 1.5 Mt in Q1 FY27, up about 3% YoY; flat-rolled products up more than 10%; electrical segment weak on deferred contractor-led projects.
Indian refined copper demand 359 kt, down 9% YoY; TC/RC at -26 to -30 cents/lb; concentrate tightness expected to persist through 2026.
Alumina prices around USD330-340/t, slightly up from historic lows, and expected to stay in this range until Middle East smelters return.

Novelis faces US Section 232 tariffs of about USD70 million in Q1 (versus USD24 million last quarter) as it imports metal while Oswego is down; management expects some tariff cost for the next couple of quarters.
Japan/Korea MJP premiums elevated due to Middle East supply disruption; expected to ease next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Novelis tariff impact of USD70 million excludable to show EBITDA/t above USD600, and why did it rise from USD24 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Novelis Steve Fisher said it was not excluded from adjusted EBITDA and advised against adding it back; tariffs stem from importing metal while Oswego is down and will persist for a few quarters. Dev Ahuja said third-party costs sit below the line as fire costs, while own-network imports do not, and declined to give specific guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the brand royalty to Birla Group Holdings affect Hindalco?
qa_highlights.answer: Satish Pai said both Novelis and Hindalco will pay a royalty of 0.25% of revenue to Birla Group Holdings, capped at INR225 crore per year, which is below Hindalco's materiality threshold and does not affect dividend or capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD300/t downstream aluminium EBITDA sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Pai said USD250/t is a more sustainable level for the rest of FY27, with the longer-term aluminium downstream target still above USD300/t; more clarity on total downstream (including copper) is due next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will Novelis leverage fall well below 4x?
qa_highlights.answer: Dev Ahuja said Novelis will be below 4x, helped by insurance recoveries, working capital release, lower ABL borrowings and higher EBITDA run-rate, after about 4.5x at end-September.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Oswego insurance recovery outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Dev Ahuja said cumulative cash impact so far is about USD1.4 billion net of recoveries, of which USD300 million has been recovered; the net cash impact is expected to settle at about USD600 million, with a couple of hundred million possibly slipping into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging position for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Pai said 21% of FY28 aluminium is hedged at USD3,160/t, with a target of about USD3,200/t; no further FY27 hedging is being added due to deep backwardation.

risks_watch: Novelis tariff costs (USD70 million in Q1) persist until supply chains are reconfigured; cash impact of Oswego fire pending insurance recovery.
India copper concentrate tightness and negative TC/RC keep pressure on smelter economics; copper smelter expansion is capital-intensive.
Elevated coal, sulphur and MJP costs; India cash costs seen rising 5-6% QoQ in Q2.
Related-party royalty (0.25% of revenue, capped at INR225 crore per year) under SEBI LODR disclosure.
USMCA status is uncertain; management does not expect a material impact.
Exceptional items of about INR300 crore at consolidated level (Ind AS vs US GAAP) expected to fall away as Oswego recovers; watch Q2 for confirmation.

We view the impact of the outage largely as a timing issue rather than a structural one.
Our long-term EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 remains unchanged.
I would say more around USD250 is a more sustainable number.

rows.why: India downstream margin seen settling near USD250/t from USD300/t in Q1 and India cash cost rising 5-6% QoQ in Q2, though India upstream EBITDA was a record INR7,390 crore at a 55% margin and Novelis cost savings run-rate is USD225 million against a USD350-400 million FY28 target.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Novelis Bay Minette 600 kt plant is on track for completion in 2026, 414 MW solar/wind and 90 MW RE-RTC are to be added in FY27, and Aditya refinery plus first 180 kt smelter phase is set for Dec 2027, but the brief does not quantify a specific FY27 quarter for each.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided higher Q2 volumes for India copper (Q1 shipments 105 kt, down 16% YoY on a smelter shutdown) and India downstream aluminium (Q1 shipments 104 kt, up 3% YoY), and Novelis volumes fell 5% to 916 kt with Oswego restarted in June.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said FY27 is a high-capex year with a strategy to double upstream capacity, and the copper smelter expansion timing is under review with smelter output expected in FY29; the brief gives no utilisation figure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: The brief shows no explicit guidance raise; India cash cost is rising 5-6% QoQ in Q2 and downstream margin is expected to normalise toward USD250/t from USD300/t.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Novelis faces USD70 million of Section 232 tariffs in Q1 (up from USD24 million), expected to persist for a couple of quarters, plus India cash costs up 5-6% QoQ in Q2 and unresolved exceptional items of about INR300 crore at consolidated level.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aditya Battery Foil and Taloja AC Fins were commissioned last quarter and are in customer qualification, and specialty alumina (precipitated hydrate) is nearing commercialisation, though no revenue figures were given.

rows.label: Novelis leverage below 4x after ~4.5x at end-September
rows.why: Novelis net debt/EBITDA is expected to start declining in Q4 and fall below 4x, helped by a USD300-400 million working capital release and insurance recoveries (USD300 million recovered of about USD1.4 billion cumulative net cash impact).

rows.label: Novelis working capital release USD300-400 million
rows.why: Management guided a USD300-400 million working capital release over the next couple of quarters, which supports the leverage decline.

rows.label: Sustained downstream margin near USD250/t
rows.why: Management sees USD250/t as the sustainable downstream margin for the rest of FY27, down from USD300/t in Q1 (downstream EBITDA INR298 crore, up 30% YoY).

tone.note: Management was confident on India upstream and downstream profitability and the Novelis recovery, but evasive on the USD70 million tariff quantification, the royalty terms and the consolidated exceptional-item treatment; analysts pushed on downstream margin sustainability and Novelis leverage.

500459|2026-03.headline: PGHH FY26 sales flat at about Rs 4,300 crore while PAT rose 19% to about Rs 850 crore on savings-funded reinvestment.
500459|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of targeted investment: sales were flat at about Rs 4,300 crore, while PAT grew 19% to about Rs 850 crore, helped by a Rs 86 crore savings programme. The call focused on the Integrated Growth Strategy, with Whisper Period Panties, Whisper Nights and Vicks launches cited as proof points. Management acknowledged category growth has been uneven, with feminine hygiene at 7-10% and healthcare at 2-3%, and flagged West Asia-linked commodity and resin cost pressure. Incoming CFO Srividya Srinivasan takes over on July 1. Few hard guidance numbers were given, and several questions on buybacks, investment plans and manufacturing were declined.

financial_highlights.metric: Structural operating margin improvement in FY26
Net profit margin expansion over 10 years

segments.name: Feminine Care
segments.commentary: Category growing 7-10%, with growth coming from varied sub-segments; Whisper is the market leader. Whisper Period Panties sold over 10 crore units and tripled the business in FY26 (as stated); Whisper Nights is about half of pad users' choice and growing ahead of the category.

segments.name: Personal Healthcare (Vicks)
segments.commentary: Category growing about 2-3%, volatile through the year and linked to monsoon timing. Vicks VapoRub returned to double-digit growth within 6 months of its all-night relief relaunch. Vicks Cough Drops offtake growing double digits this year, with volume and volume share up on a past-3-month basis.

guidance_outlook: Management expects some near-term challenges to continue, citing macro headwinds, West Asia conflict and inflation.
Feminine hygiene category expected to grow at late single digits this year; long-term category growth expected at mid to high single digits.
Multi-year savings master plans being built for each business unit, intended to fund reinvestment and margin expansion.
Management said it would not guide on price-sensitive matters; no quantitative FY27 sales or margin guidance was given.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or utilisation figures were disclosed on the call.
Manufacturing footprint and future investment plans were raised in Q&A but were not answered.
demand_pricing: Crude and resin prices have risen 30-50% due to the West Asia conflict; the company said it has not gone out of stock.
Rural consumption still exceeds urban, but a softening trend is visible due to inflation; non-food inflation is below the RBI 4% medium-term target.
More than 50 new players have entered feminine hygiene in the last 10 years, including regional and D2C brands.
Healthcare category has declined for many quarters post-COVID, with early signs of recovery in recent quarters.
Qcomm: one in four consumers buying period products are choosing panties, where Whisper is #1.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue growth slowed over the last 5 years despite ad spends, distribution expansion and launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited fast-changing consumer needs, shifts in media and retail, and very high competitiveness; it said it is investing in innovation, communication and Nights and Panties segments.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company not launching new-age products in feminine hygiene?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to its Nights and Period Panties launches and upgrades to existing lines across benefits and sizes, with Whisper Period Panties positioned as the segment leader.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins being optimised at the expense of growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said flat sales came after reinvestment and that savings are used to fund product, package and demand generation; green shoots are visible in focus portfolio areas.

qa_highlights.question: How are West Asia-linked cost pressures being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said crude and resin prices are up 30-50%, supply continuity has been maintained, and savings programmes are being accelerated to offset costs.

qa_highlights.question: Questions on CEO/CFO turnover and management tenure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said strategy has stayed constant across leadership changes and that a grow-from-within talent model ensures succession continuity.

qa_highlights.question: Questions on buybacks, parent company investment and manufacturing expansion.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to answer, citing unpublished price-sensitive information.

risks_watch: Top-line stagnation: FY26 sales flat despite investments; watch whether volume growth returns in FY27.
Commodity and resin cost inflation from the West Asia conflict, which could erode the margin gains.
Intensifying competition from regional and D2C players in feminine hygiene and healthcare.

rows.why: Wealth management business was launched in Q4 FY26, but no further product launches or timelines were disclosed.

rows.label: ECL transition impact
rows.why: Impact is still being assessed; draft guidance allows the INR 456 crore-linked floating provision to be used during transition, but the quantum is not yet known.

rows.label: Retail home loan pricing and retail growth drag
rows.why: Retail home loans priced at about 7.15% (15-year) are unattractive, the retail book is flat YoY, and management says it will not chase volume at current levels.

rows.label: Asset quality at decade best
rows.why: GNPA at a decade-low 1.62% and NNPA at an all-time low 0.37% with provision coverage up 141 bps QoQ to 76.55%, supporting credit cost stability.

tone.note: Management was confident on CASA (up 8.26% QoQ to INR 1,03,390 crore), NIM and asset quality, but cautious on forward growth and ECL, leaving credit cost and cost-to-income guidance unchanged; analysts pushed on margin outlook, LCR decline, gold loan LTV and Middle East exposure.

500470|2026-03.headline: Tata Steel FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 35% YoY to Rs 34,848 crore; FY27 cost savings target Rs 7,100 crore and capex step-up to ~Rs 20,000 crore.
500470|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 63,270 crore and EBITDA Rs 9,953 crore (16% margin), helped by higher India realisations, volumes and cost savings. India EBITDA grew 17% YoY to Rs 34,272 crore at a 24% margin, and UK plus Netherlands EBITDA turned positive for the full year. Management guided Q1 FY27 realisations up about Rs 6,000/t in India, £80/t in UK and €80/t in Netherlands. The main overhang is the Netherlands coke and gas plant (CGP) closure, which has led auditors to flag a material uncertainty on TSN's going concern, plus a delayed UK EAF grid connection.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 9,439 crore on revenue of Rs 38,448 crore

financial_highlights.change: Operating cash flow before capex and dividend ~Rs 29,254 crore vs ~Rs 17,700 crore

financial_highlights.value: Rs 10,868 crore (India ~Rs 3,927 crore, UK ~Rs 1,958 crore, Netherlands ~Rs 4,983 crore)

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: EBITDA Rs 34,272 crore in FY26 (+17% YoY) at 24% margin, in line with 10-year average; crude steel output ~23 Mt (+8% YoY), with Kalinganagar phase 2 ramp complete. NINL Q4 EBITDA Rs 402 crore (+15% QoQ, ~27% margin).

segments.name: UK (TSUK)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA -£48 million, improved £15 million QoQ; FY26 EBITDA -£217 million, narrowed £168 million YoY. Annual deliveries ~2.2 Mt; losses around £98/t cited.

segments.name: Netherlands (TSN)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA €58 million (€34/t), held back by lower realisations; FY26 EBITDA €267 million, almost tripled YoY. Liquid steel ~6.7 Mt and deliveries ~6.1 Mt; DSP plant shut after emission exceedances.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 realisations expected ~Rs 6,000/t higher than Q4 in India, of which ~30% in Q1 and ~70% in Q2 for auto contracts; ~£80/t higher in UK and ~€80/t higher in Netherlands.
Q1 FY27 coal cost up ~$15/t in India and ~$10/t in Netherlands; iron ore up ~$5/t in Netherlands. Management expects India and UK margin expansion and Netherlands margin compression.
FY27 cost transformation savings target ~Rs 7,100 crore vs FY26.
FY27 consolidated capex ~Rs 20,000 crore (from ~Rs 14,000 crore in FY26), over 60% in India.
FY27 volume at least 2 Mt higher than FY26, mostly India, driven by Kalinganagar ramp-up.
UK targeted to turn EBITDA positive during FY27; UK safeguard revision from 1 July 2026 (quota cut ~60%, tariff 25% to 50%) expected to lift prices.
NINL merger with Tata Steel to complete in FY27; NINL expansion FID expected July-September 2026, target start 2029-30.
Dividend of Rs 4 per share proposed.
capex_capacity: Kalinganagar 5 MTPA ramp-up complete; Ludhiana 0.75 MTPA scrap-based EAF commissioned and ramping (about 0.5 Mt in FY27 volumes).
NINL 5 MTPA expansion: FEL3 advanced, FID expected in July-September 2026, target 2029-30; site planned as a 10 Mt site.
India capex projects include HRPGL at Tarapur (0.8 MTPA), tinplate expansion (0.3-0.4 MTPA), Jamshedpur coke oven projects, tubes and wires, and mining projects.
UK ~3 MTPA scrap-based EAF: demolition complete; National Grid connectivity delayed, with the delay now estimated at 6-8 months or more, down from an initial 18 months to 12 months.
Netherlands: DSP plant suspended after emission exceedances, restart targeted later in May pending approvals; CGP closure timeline still under discussion with regulators.
Maharashtra greenfield site: land identified, update expected in about three months; potential 6-10 Mt.
demand_pricing: India demand outlook: management previously expected 8-10% steel demand growth but would recalibrate if GDP growth slows; auto strong, construction slowed, MSME stress noted.
Q1 FY27 price trend: prices rose in March-April-May; long products softening from secondary producers, flats firm on higher China prices (+$20-25/t in 3-4 weeks) and better export options.

Retail/branded: Tata Tiscon retail sales above 200,000 t/month (up from 100,000-120,000 t/month); Tata Steelium cold-rolled volumes ~28% YoY; Aashiyana online platform GMV ~Rs 5,000 crore, sold at Tata Steel margins.
UK safeguard: slabs excluded from quotas; UK prices had been ~£100/t below Europe and have now caught up to slightly above.
India slab transfers to UK to rise to ~1.8 Mt from ~1.2 Mt; system EBITDA ~Rs 12,000/t on slabs (Rs 7,000-8,000/t market basis plus UK share).

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost impact of closing the Netherlands coke and gas plants and buying coke?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed a cost penalty from losing coke oven gas and adding freight, partly offset by lower CO2; net impact depends on timing, with coke sourced from India or elsewhere. No quantified figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did auditors flag material uncertainty on TSN going concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cause is a post-balance-sheet letter from environmental agencies on intent to revoke permits without dates or pathway; closure must be planned and safe, and CGP shutdown is expected to take time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UK EAF commissioning delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay of 6-8 months or more after plant build; initial estimate of 18 months has come down to about 12 months, with efforts to reduce further and trials planned with one line connection.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation and cost guidance for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: India ~Rs 6,000/t higher QoQ, largely from prices up to May; auto contracts partly in Q1 (30%) and Q2 (70%). Other West Asia-related cost impacts not quantified yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why not faster brownfield expansion in India versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited optionality to reach 45-50 Mt on existing sites, a new approach of announcing projects only after FEL3 and approvals, and a shift of value pools to downstream amid rising iron ore and coal costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TMILL stake increase about?
qa_highlights.answer: TMILL stake rises from 51% to 74% with NYK holding the balance; TMILL has ~55 rakes and about 80% of revenue from ground and rail logistics. Slurry pipeline and waterways expansion planned.

risks_watch: Netherlands CGP closure timeline, permit revocation risk and cost penalty from buying coke; TSN going concern material uncertainty.
UK EAF power connection delay (6-8+ months) and whether UK turns EBITDA positive in FY27 given Middle East energy costs.
West Asia impact on energy, freight and inputs (propane shortage hit galvanising, tinplate and colour lines); costs not yet quantified for Q1 FY27.
Long product softness from secondary producers and possible demand slowdown from weaker GDP outlook and construction slowdown.
NINL FID (July-September 2026) and Maharashtra site update in ~3 months; mass claim defence in the Netherlands is in progress.
Iron ore cost increases and post-2030 captive lease bidding; ~$1 billion offshore ECB exposure is hedged.
500470|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on India growth, cost savings and pricing, with a clear upbeat tone on Q1 realisations. Noticeably cautious and at times evasive on the Netherlands CGP closure, the timing of the NINL and Maharashtra expansions, and the Q1 West Asia cost impact, which management declined to quantify.
key_quotes: Tata Steel delivered a strong performance in FY2026, with improved margins expanding across operating geographies despite subdued pricing and challenges during the year.

We have also enhanced our working capital efficiency and released around Rs 6,000 crores of cash during the year especially in India and Netherlands through very focused management of working capital.
So, we expect them to take care of themselves.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: Q1-Q2 FY27 (India and UK); Netherlands compresses
rows.why: India Q4 standalone EBITDA Rs 9,439 crore with realisations up ~Rs 6,000/t and cost savings target ~Rs 7,100 crore in FY27 (FY26 achieved Rs 10,868 crore at 95% of plan), partly offset by coal up ~$15/t in India and ~$10/t in Netherlands.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY28-FY30; NINL 5 MTPA target 2029-30, UK EAF after grid con

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 India volumes at least 2 Mt above FY26 (~23 Mt crude steel in FY26, +8% YoY), mostly from the Kalinganagar phase 2 ramp, which is complete, plus ~0.5 Mt from Ludhiana EAF.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: FY27; NINL FID Jul-Sep 2026; Maharashtra site update in ~3 m
rows.why: FY27 consolidated capex raised to ~Rs 20,000 crore from ~Rs 14,000 crore in FY26 (over 60% India), with NINL FID and a Maharashtra greenfield site (potential 6-10 Mt) both pending.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 FY27 realisations guided ~Rs 6,000/t higher in India (30% in Q1, 70% in Q2 for auto), £80/t in UK and €80/t in Netherlands, and UK safeguard revision from 1 July 2026 (quota cut ~60%, tariff 25% to 50%) is expected to lift prices; flats prices up $20-25/t in 3-4 weeks.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 FY27 West Asia energy, freight and propane cost impacts are not quantified, Netherlands CGP closure adds coke-purchase and freight penalty with no figure, and the Netherlands going-concern uncertainty is flagged; long product prices are softening from secondary producers.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: HRPGL Tarapur 0.8 MTPA and tinplate expansion (0.3-0.4 MTPA) are planned, but no launch dates were given; Tata Tiscon retail sales already above 200,000 t/month (from 100,000-120,000).

rows.label: UK EBITDA positive in FY27
rows.why: UK Q4 EBITDA -£48 million improved £15 million QoQ, FY26 EBITDA -£217 million; Q1 FY27 realisation +£80/t and UK safeguard revision from 1 July 2026 could lift prices, but UK EAF connection is delayed 6-8+ months and Middle East energy costs are a risk.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA falling
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA is 2.3x at FY26 year-end (vs 3.3x two years back), FY26 free cash flow Rs 10,738 crore, but FY27 capex steps up to ~Rs 20,000 crore from ~Rs 14,000 crore.

rows.label: Netherlands CGP closure and TSN going concern
rows.why: Auditors flagged material uncertainty on TSN going concern after environmental agencies signalled intent to revoke permits with no dates; DSP plant is suspended with restart targeted in May, and CGP closure timeline is still under discussion with regulators.

tone.note: Management was confident on India growth, cost savings (FY26 Rs 10,868 crore, 95% of plan) and Q1 realisations, but cautious or evasive on the Netherlands CGP closure, NINL and Maharashtra timing, and the unquantified Q1 West Asia cost impact.

500470|2026-06.headline: Tata Steel 1QFY27 consolidated EBITDA Rs 9,370 crore, up Rs 2,400/t YoY; India margin 27% despite lower volumes and a Netherlands DSP shutdown.
500470|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was about Rs 60,794 crore and EBITDA Rs 9,370 crore, with consolidated EBITDA per ton tracking near Rs 13,000 (about 15% margin) after about Rs 1,200 crore of West Asia-related unplanned costs. India delivered EBITDA of about Rs 9,900 crore (up 32% YoY) on crude steel of 5.76 Mt and deliveries of 5.17 Mt, with realisations up Rs 5,990/t QoQ. The Netherlands was weak after the Direct Sheet Plant shutdown from early April and chrome-emission issues, with TSN EBITDA about €4 million. Management guided 2Q India NSR down about Rs 1,500/t, UK EBITDA breakeven pushed possibly by a quarter, and is reassessing the Netherlands DRI-EAF investment case.

financial_highlights.change: Up Rs 2,400/t YoY and Rs 1,490/t QoQ per ton
From -£48 million in 4Q; fourth straight quarter of improvement
Up 3% QoQ; NSR up about £91/t, costs up about £54/t
Revenue about €1.4 billion; revenue/t up €87, costs/t up €118

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt / net debt to EBITDA

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 45,950 crore (incl. cash about Rs 13,221 crore)

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Crude steel 5.76 Mt (lower QoQ due to shutdowns and operational snags) and deliveries 5.17 Mt, with inventory rebuild. Standalone costs rose about Rs 6,700/t on lower volumes; India is about 75% of group crude steel.

segments.name: Automotive & Speciality / Branded
segments.commentary: Best-ever 1Q volumes in automotive and speciality, high-end sales up 21% YoY. Tata Tiscon volumes up 33% YoY; Tata Steelium volumes up 34% YoY, helped by the Kalinganagar cold rolling mill. Digital platforms Aashiyana and DigECA GMV about Rs 2,200 crore, up 61% YoY.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Deliveries about 0.5 Mt; EBITDA loss narrowed to -£27 million. Port Talbot pickle line fire on 3 June 2026 cost about 10,000 t volume and about £5 million EBITDA in 1Q. Tariff-free quotas cut and a 50% tariff applied beyond quota from 1 July.

segments.name: Netherlands (TSN)
segments.commentary: Liquid steel 1.55 Mt and deliveries 1.4 Mt. DSP (about 20% of output, 1.4 Mt capacity) shut since early April, and finished-steel loss for almost the full quarter from chrome emission exceedance. Four-week trial run from about 5 August; management expects 2Q volumes and EBITDA above 1Q.

segments.name: NINL
segments.commentary: EBITDA about Rs 498 crore at 29% margin. Board approved 4.8 MTPA long-products expansion (investment Rs 33,873 crore), taking the site to 6.2 MTPA; NINL merger with Tata Steel expected by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: India 2Q NSR guided about Rs 1,500/t lower than 1Q; rupee crore EBITDA expected better in 2Q than 1Q on higher volumes, with some margin compression.
UK NSR guided up £70-80/t in 2Q over 1Q, but not all flows to margin as substrate costs also rise; spreads to expand in 2Q. UK EBITDA breakeven still the goal, possibly slipping from 2Q to 3Q or 4Q.
Netherlands NSR guided up about €10/t in 2Q (vs €70/t delivered in 1Q); spread broadly flat; 2Q volumes and EBITDA expected above 1Q.
2Q coking coal cost up about $5/t in India and $10/t in Netherlands, with coking coal at about $184/t.
Depreciation rises by about Rs 300 crore per quarter (Rs 1,200 crore a year) from accelerated amortisation of mining and PPE assets ahead of 2030 re-auction.
NINL 4.8 MTPA expansion commissioning within 48 months from zero date of 1 August 2026; Ludhiana EAF full-year numbers expected next year.
capex_capacity: Board granted final investment approval for 4.8 MTPA NINL long-products expansion (Rs 33,873 crore), taking NINL to 6.2 MTPA; overall NINL plan is 10 MTPA.
Kalinganagar phase 2 (5 MTPA) and 0.75 MTPA Ludhiana EAF are ramping up; Cuttack Superflex weld mesh line commissioned.

Tinplate expansion of 0.3 MTPA and 0.74 MTPA hot-roll pickling and galvanising project on track within 30 months; 0.5 MTPA Jamshedpur combi mill commissioned and ramping up; about 0.42 MTPA tube capacity to be added in FY27 via asset-light route.
UK 3 MTPA scrap-based EAF: groundworks done, 35% piling complete, major OEM orders placed, about half of equipment made; National Grid connection delay flagged.
Maharashtra site: about 3,000+ acres, eventually about 15 MTPA in three 5 MTPA blast furnaces, engineering not started. MK B iron ore mine expansion of 15 MTPA in phases.
demand_pricing: India long products weakened in July as monsoon slowed construction; flat products supported by strong auto demand.

UK: safeguard revisions cut tariff-free quotas by about 3.3-3.4 Mt from 1 July with 50% tariff beyond quota; management wants quotas revisited for galvanised, tubular and packaging steels where quotas are 70-80% of demand.

EU: European prices stuck around €700/t with weak demand and above-average inventories; management expects phased uplift from November contract renewals as EU safeguard cuts imports to 18 Mt of 30 Mt.
Chinese steel exports of about 9-10 million tons a month are weighing on international prices.
Shipbuilding approvals obtained; about 100 kt expected this year, potential 0.5 Mt. Data-centre steel and storage solutions being pursued in India and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EU restocking cycle drive a significant European price uptick, given prices stuck near €700/t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects uplift from the November contract renewal, driven by CBAM and quotas (18 Mt of 30 Mt imports allowed), but in phases rather than a sharp rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is UK EBITDA breakeven in 2H still achievable given quotas and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Still on course, though it may slip one quarter to 3Q or 4Q; UK prices are moving closer to EU levels, and November contract renewals will be the test.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Maharashtra capex trimmed to 5 MTPA from 6 MTPA, and why is NINL costlier than Kalinganagar?
qa_highlights.answer: Land supports about 15 MTPA eventually via three 5 MTPA blast furnaces; NINL is treated as greenfield with enabling works, and imported equipment costs are affected by the FX rate.

qa_highlights.question: How much captive iron ore post-2030, and what cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Captive mines currently produce under 5 Mt and are expected to reach 30-35 Mt; captive share will be set by economics, with the 50% target not fixed and purchases considered at high premiums.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Netherlands DSP issue and the Dutch regulatory risk not resolved, and what is the DRI-EAF status?
qa_highlights.answer: DSP restarts for a four-week trial from 5 August after roller changes; DRI-EAF is being reassessed with regulators, with coke-oven closure possibly advanced to 2028-29 and slag conditions unresolved.

qa_highlights.question: Expected NSR and cost movement for July and 2Q?
qa_highlights.answer: India NSR about Rs 1,500/t lower in 2Q than 1Q; UK up £70-80/t; Netherlands up about €10/t; coking coal up $5/t India and $10/t Netherlands.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Accelerated amortisation of mining and PPE assets ahead of the 2030 re-auction adds about Rs 300 crore a quarter.

risks_watch: Netherlands DSP restart: four-week trial from about 5 August; whether regulators allow running beyond the trial, and whether the chrome-emission issue is fully closed.

Netherlands regulatory exposure: criminal case on undercooked coke pushes (hearing reported for 20 November), slag conditions in the JLoI, and possible coke-oven closure advanced to 2028-29; DRI-EAF investment case under reassessment.

UK EBITDA breakeven timing may slip from 2Q to 3Q or 4Q; November contract renewals are the test of whether UK and EU price increases stick; UK quotas for galvanised, tubular and packaging steel still seen as too generous.
India 2Q NSR guided about Rs 1,500/t lower, with long products weak in monsoon; margin compression expected even as rupee EBITDA improves on volumes.

Cost headwinds: West Asia-related energy, freight and raw material costs (about Rs 1,200 crore unplanned in 1Q); coking coal up $5/t India and $10/t Netherlands in 2Q; iron ore costs expected to rise as captive mine share changes post-2030.

Capex and execution: Maharashtra capex recalibrated to 5 MTPA units from 6 MTPA; NINL 4.8 MTPA project (Rs 33,873 crore) to be commissioned within 48 months; UK EAF faces National Grid connection delay; depreciation rising about Rs 300 crore a quarter.
key_quotes: So, we are looking at how can you deliver an EBITDA margin close to what we are delivering today even if the iron ore prices go up.
So, we feel that the cost of producing steel in India will go up because everyone's buying iron ore at these prices.
It may be pushed by one quarter and may not be in 2Q but 3Q or 4Q.

So, we are currently reassessing the situation with all stakeholders to understand the investability of the DRI – EAF, the regulatory framework within which there is not just an investment case but also a sustenance case.
500470|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on India volumes, margins and balance sheet (net debt to EBITDA 2.3x, within 2.5-3x range), but cautious and open-ended on the Netherlands, where the DSP restart, chrome emissions, the criminal case and the DRI-EAF investment case are all described as unresolved. Management was also measured on UK breakeven timing (may slip one quarter) and declined to give a numerical iron ore cost estimate, citing too many variables.

rows.why: India 2Q NSR guided about Rs 1,500/t lower than 1Q with some margin compression, partly offset by higher volumes and UK NSR up £70-80/t, Netherlands NSR up about €10/t; coking coal up $5/t India and $10/t Netherlands, and depreciation up about Rs 300 crore a quarter, so rupee EBITDA better but per-ton margin not clearly expanding.

rows.why: Kalinganagar phase 2 (5 MTPA) and 0.75 MTPA Ludhiana EAF are already ramping up, and 0.5 MTPA Jamshedpur combi mill is commissioned; the 0.3 MTPA tinplate and 0.74 MTPA pickling/galvanising project is on track within 30 months, and NINL 4.8 MTPA (Rs 33,873 crore) got final approval, but its commissioning is up to 48 months away.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects Netherlands 2Q volumes and EBITDA above 1Q after the DSP restart trial from about 5 August (DSP is about 20% of TSN output, 1.4 Mt capacity), and India volumes are expected higher in 2Q after 1Q shutdowns (crude 5.76 Mt, deliveries 5.17 Mt), though no group volume growth number was given and long products weakened in July.

rows.why: Board already accorded final approval for the NINL 4.8 MTPA expansion (Rs 33,873 crore) and the Maharashtra plan (about 15 MTPA eventually via three 5 MTPA blast furnaces) is in the pipeline with land secured, while engineering there has not started; further project-level announcements are likely but the big one is already approved.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.when: next 2-3 quarters (trial from about 5 Aug; hearing reported
rows.why: DSP (about 20% of TSN output, 1.4 Mt capacity) restarts on a four-week trial, the DRI-EAF investment case is under reassessment, and coke-oven closure could be advanced to 2028-29, so the outcome is conditional.

500472|2026-03.headline: SKF India Q4 FY26 sales rose 3% QoQ to INR 5.55 bn, but PBT margin fell to about 9% after Q3 one-off gains; management guides 11-12% PBT margin.
500472|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 (Jan-Mar 2026) sales were a record INR 5.55 bn, up about 3% QoQ and about 14.8% YoY, driven by cars, 2-wheelers and powertrains, with a drop in distribution. Profit before tax margin fell to about 9% as Q3 had one-off gains from forex, fixed-deposit interest and employee cost provision reversals. FY26 sales grew about 12.7% to INR 20.3 bn with OE up about 20%, while full-year PBT margin fell to about 12.3% on demerger costs, mix and discounts. Management pointed to 11-12% PBT margin as the near-term sustainable level and said cash conversion was about 85%.

segments.name: Automotive OE
segments.commentary: About 66% of Q4 sales and the main growth driver, with FY26 OE sales up about 20%. Management said the growth came from OEM, and OEM margins are structurally different from aftermarket.

segments.name: Distribution / aftermarket
segments.commentary: About 20% of Q4 sales; declined YoY in FY26. Management said volumes were held flat but net sales fell due to discounts to defend share against competition.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 8% of Q4 sales; broadly steady but slightly lower. Domestic demand is prioritised given limited capacity, and overseas demand is served from nearby plants.

segments.name: SKF Industrial (traded)
segments.commentary: About 6% of Q4 sales. Automotive buys traded product from SKF Industrial (medium DGBB and tapered roller bearings) to cover capacity shortfall; traded purchases were about 15-20% of revenue in Q3-Q4 per analyst.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable company-level PBT margin of about 11-12% in the near term; long-term focus is on improving it further.
Management expects margins to return toward prior levels after a couple of quarters once one-offs and transition costs fade.
Demerger costs in Q4 were minimal and no further demerger-related costs are expected.
Raw material (steel) cost pass-through has begun with a couple of OEMs and aftermarket; near-term gross margin pressure from pass-through lag acknowledged.
Automotive revenue growth expected at about 6-8% CAGR to 2028, per management.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR 500 crore over FY26-FY28, with about INR 200 crore in FY26, spilling into Q1 FY27.
Capex aims to bring trading from SKF Industrial into in-house automotive capacity; this does not add revenue beyond existing trading revenue.
Automotive is short of capacity; two new product lines are coming up at Haridwar in 2026.
Automotive plant in Pune is common with SKF Industrial; SKF India receives rent and service charges for space used by Industrial until its new factory is ready.
Localisation above 90% in automotive, which management says will continue.
demand_pricing: Strong order book and wins in electric motors and wheel-hub bearings, with launches in FY27; order book described as running to about 2030.
EV share of 2-wheeler business is about 50% per MD; EV revenue mix is about 6% of 2-wheeler and about 4% of passenger vehicle sales.
Aftermarket discounts used to hold share against competition; price increases in aftermarket have started.
Top 5 customers are close to 50% of revenue; top 10 about 70%. Bajaj is the largest customer, followed by Mahindra and Tata.
White spaces named: unitised wheel bearings for SCV/LCV and low-friction, low-weight transmission products for CAFE-3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin going forward into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 11-12% PBT margin is achievable near term; Q4 demerger costs were small and Q3 one-off gains distorted the comparison.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material inflation be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said steel-linked price increases are recoverable under OEM agreements; recovery has started with a couple of customers, with aftermarket increases also starting. Lag means near-term gross margin pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What are the arrangements with SKF Industrial (trading, rent, service charges)?

Network touch points at 2,137 (1,177 MHCV, 960 LCV) after adding 33 in Q1, with focus on North and East.
Optare debt of about GBP 50 million remaining; plan to repay GBP 25 million this year and GBP 25 million next year.
demand_pricing: Domestic MHCV industry grew 13% YoY in Q1 (May about 1-2%, June above 20%, July above 20%). Growth drivers: GST recalibration, replacement of BS3/BS4 fleets, financing and infrastructure.
Price increase in Q1 was about 1.2-1.25%; cumulative FY27 price increases are about 2.25% for MHCV and more than 3.5% for LCV.
Commodity costs (steel, natural rubber) remain elevated; price hikes and cost savings offset about half of the Q1 commodity increase each; inventory accounting offset the rest.
Competitive intensity in the MAV segment is rising. The new air-suspension multi-axle truck offers 4 tonnes extra payload, versus 2 tonnes from a competitor product.
Management's BS7 view: not before 2031, possibly 2032.

qa_highlights.question: What was the gross RM headwind in Q1, and how much pricing offset it? What is the pending impact for Q2?

Price increases and cost savings each offset about 50% of the commodity increase. Remaining inventory-related costs will flow through later, but will be modest.

qa_highlights.question: What are the mix and truck demand outlook for the rest of the year?

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and export outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex was about INR900-1,000 crore in the last two years and will rise over the next 2-3 years. Exports should recover as RAK ramps to 800 units a month; SAARC and Africa grew 40-60%.

qa_highlights.question: Is competitive intensity rising in the MAV segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says its air-suspension product was a 2.5-3 year engineering project, not a reaction to competitors. It is the first such launch in India, offering 4 tonnes of extra payload.

qa_highlights.question: Can non-MHCV businesses cover fixed costs?

Inventory-led margin benefit is partly timing; the deferred cost will flow into P&L in later quarters.

500480|2026-03.headline: Cummins India FY26 sales rose 18% to INR11,950 crore and Q4 PBT before exceptionals rose 20% to INR820 crore, with data centres at about 35% of Q4 domestic power gen revenue.
500480|2026-03.overview: FY26 sales grew 18% YoY to INR11,950 crore, with domestic sales up 19% to INR9,961 crore and exports up 12% to INR1,989 crore. Q4 FY26 sales were INR2,963 crore, up 23% YoY but down 1% QoQ, and PBT before exceptional items rose 20% YoY to INR820 crore. Power generation domestic sales led growth, while industrial domestic sales were flat for the year. segments.name: Distribution domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR3,278 crore, up 22% YoY. Q4 sales INR766 crore, up 21% YoY but down 18% QoQ. Management said price contributed little to growth.

segments.name: Industrial domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR1,650 crore, down 1% YoY. Q4 sales INR381 crore, up 1% YoY and down 18% QoQ; Q4 split was construction INR164 crore, rail INR111 crore, compressor INR59 crore, with the rest mining and defence.

segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR984 crore, up 20% YoY. Q4 sales INR217 crore, down 1% YoY and 7% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 and Q4 power gen revenue came from data centres?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 hyperscaler revenue disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR250 crore of value in the quarter, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will larger engines (QSK78/QSK95) change the competitive landscape and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: QSK60 remains the near-term product for the next 2 years, and QSK78 looks more likely than QSK95. Management said no competitor makes 95-litre engines in India, and its value proposition covers service and solutions beyond cost, so margin impact is hard to call.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the commodity impact and how fast is it passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity increases are passed on with a lag. Order-book timing creates the challenge. DEF is a very small part of distribution. HHP lead times are 3 to 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity expansion planned, given 70% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No major capex is planned. Management is spending on line modernisation and output increases, and can tap global parent plants via an integrated supply chain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for BESS?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest and inquiries are high, but there is no sales pipeline yet and no local supply chain. Management is not sharing a contribution estimate or customer cohorts.

qa_highlights.question: Is price or volume driving growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is volume-led. Price and content gains apply mainly to CPCB IV+, and distribution growth comes from new solutions, not price.

500480|2026-06.headline: Cummins India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR3,375 crore, but pre-exceptional PBT fell 0.7% to INR721 crore as commodity inflation hit margins.

Exports were flat YoY at INR521 crore, with high-horsepower exports up 16% but low-horsepower exports down 20%. Profit before tax before exceptional items was INR721 crore, marginally lower YoY, as steel, pig iron, aluminium and copper inflation, freight and West Asia disruption weighed on margins. Management took one price increase at the start of Q2 FY27 and said it had not yet been absorbed by the market; no price hike was taken in Q1. Data centres drove a large share of power generation growth.

segments.commentary: INR886 crore, +14% YoY and +16% QoQ, slowing from a 20%-plus five-year CAGR. Management said the slowdown reflects a higher base, parts availability and supply disruption, and reiterated 20% growth potential.

segments.commentary: INR458 crore, +10% YoY. Construction INR148 crore (flat YoY), rail INR145 crore (strong order book), compressor INR52 crore, marine INR50 crore; mining, defence and others the remainder.

segments.commentary: INR521 crore, flat YoY. HHP INR296 crore (+16% YoY), LHP INR180 crore (-20% YoY). Middle East weak due to West Asia crisis; Europe and Asia Pacific were the main growth markets.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity increases are unprecedented and it could not say whether margins would hit historic highs. It expects margins to improve as cost management gets better.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise sharply with flat headcount?

500493|2026-03.headline: Bharat Forge FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% to INR 16,812 crore, but standalone revenue fell 5% to INR 8,396 crore on US and CV demand headwinds.
500493|2026-03.overview: Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR 16,812 crore (up 11%) and EBITDA INR 2,921 crore (up about 6%), with consolidated net debt-to-equity at 0.41x. Standalone revenue fell about 5% YoY to INR 8,396 crore and standalone EBITDA was INR 2,312 crore (27.5% margin), though Q4 standalone revenue rose 8.5% QoQ to INR 2,260 crore on export recovery and domestic auto strength. Management is restructuring the German steel subsidiary (CDP Bharat Forge) over roughly 15-18 months, is taking an e-mobility investment write-off, and is pushing growth in aerospace, defence and JSA castings. Management guided to about 25% growth for India operations in FY27, barring geopolitical shocks.

500520|2026-06.headline: M&M Q1 FY27: consolidated PAT up 34% and ROE at 23%, with Auto margins hit by 400-500 bps commodity inflation and Farm hit by steel and rubber.

Mahindra Finance profit rose 78% on NIM recovery to 7.3% and a pivot back to growth, while Tech Mahindra profit rose 28% and Growth Gems profit rose about 3x. Auto price increases of about 2.7% on average were taken in July, and Q1 is described as the low point for Auto margins. Management stayed cautiously optimistic, and Auto management said the June commodity trend was easing while the July hedging loss of about 85 bps weighed on Q1.

500530|2026-03.headline: Bosch Ltd to acquire related-party Bosch Chassis Systems India (RBIC) for INR9,068.7 crore, ~10.6x FY25 EV/EBITDA, targeted close by end-Q1 FY27.
500530|2026-03.overview: This transcript covers two investor calls on April 13, 2026, about the proposed acquisition of Bosch Chassis Systems India Pvt Ltd (RBIC), a group company, not a quarterly results call; management said it was in silent period and would not discuss quarterly results. RBIC posted FY25 revenue of about INR4,000 crore and a 19.3% EBITDA margin, with 9M FY26 revenue of about INR3,500 crore. Pro forma FY25 revenue for Bosch Ltd rises about 22% to INR22,000 crore and EBITDA margin improves from 12.8% to 13.9%, with about 5% pro forma EPS accretion. The deal is almost all cash, funded from existing funds and internal accruals, with a small preferential allotment to Robert Bosch Netherlands and Robert Bosch US, and shareholder voting runs April 9 to May 8, 2026.

Pro forma FY25 EBITDA margin (Bosch Ltd)

segments.commentary: Covers ABS, ESP, occupant safety sensors and controllers, EV new braking systems (iBooster, integrated power brakes) and conventional actuation; about one-third two-wheeler and the rest passenger and commercial vehicles per management's rough estimate. Three plants (Chakan, Manesar, Sanand) and about 2,000 people including contract workers.

segments.name: Bosch Ltd - power solutions and aftermarket
segments.commentary: Retains powertrain/propulsion and mobility aftermarket. Management said the portfolios are complementary with no overlap. Bosch Automotive Electronics (captive contract manufacturer, low margin, high capex) is excluded from this deal and is under review.

Target to complete acquisition by end of Q1 FY27, subject to shareholder approval.
Management expects to hold margins steady for about 5 years and to fund all major OEM projects through their 2031 launches.
Capex for the target guided at about 1.5%-3.5% of net sales in the business case; no firm capex figure given.
Dividend distribution policy of 55%-85% of PAT reiterated.
capex_capacity: Target's main plant is in Chakan; a large plant in Jharkhand; Manesar is an assembly unit and Sanand a warehouse, with management saying the current capacity is near max in its current locations.
Expansion is mostly brownfield, using idle lines from the Bosch global network (second-hand, pre-run lines) for faster ramp-up.
Each e-axle line produces about 150,000 units; the e-axle market is small in India and the 50:50 JV with Tata Autocomp is intended to consolidate volumes.
Management says it will add capacity only against legislation or confirmed OEM programmes.
demand_pricing: Management said the order book is very full, with a project pipeline for 4-5 years, and that no orders have been lost so far.
Two-wheeler ABS: management says Bosch holds a very high, market-leading share; a below-125cc ABS mandate is still under consideration with no new update.
Margins expected to face some pressure from OEMs wanting customized solutions and from cost-down pressure in ABS for the 2-wheeler segment, but management expects to hold margins steady.
Management said it is the market leader in passenger car ABS/ESP and the most advanced ESP is 10th generation.
Localization is over 90% of child parts for some Bosch Ltd products, according to management.

qa_highlights.question: Why was RBIC chosen now, and why not Bosch Automotive Electronics (related-party exposure)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RBIC is powertrain-agnostic and margin-accretive from day one. The automotive electronics entity is a captive, low-margin, capex-heavy contract manufacturer and is excluded for now but under ongoing review.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix and synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly one-third two-wheeler and the rest cars and commercial vehicles. No synergies counted in the business case; they will be reviewed in post-merger integration.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the margin jump (gross margin from ~34% to ~40%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited scale, localization of products and child parts, legislation-led volume, modular platforms, and idle lines transferred from the Bosch network, with stable quality and productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a preferential issue of only about INR8.8 crore disclosed and not the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: The company secretary said the announcement covered only the preferential issue and that the acquisition details were UPSI before the board meeting. The questioner challenged the disclosure, and management said it would improve governance practice.

qa_highlights.question: Cash, funding and balance sheet after deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash consideration is covered and both companies will be debt-free post-deal. The company did not disclose the target's H1 cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Order book at RBIC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the order book as very full, with a 4-5 year project pipeline and good market share in all categories.

risks_watch: Related-party transaction exposure is rising: Bosch Automotive Electronics supplies to both entities on a cost-plus transfer price basis, and royalty terms are described as 'very similar'.
Governance: questions were raised on the adequacy of the April 1, 2026 board-meeting intimation, and the company was asked to improve disclosure.
Shareholder approval through the voting window ending May 8, 2026, and completion targeted by end-Q1 FY27.
Management views on the 2-wheeler ABS mandate for sub-125cc bikes remain unconfirmed; the deal business case excludes unlegislated upside.
Margin pressure in ABS for 2-wheelers and from Chinese competitors; the transfer price and cost-based structure will need monitoring post-close.
RBIC cash flow and capex figures were not disclosed; the cash flow figures stated as of 9M FY26 are unconfirmed.

500530|2026-06.headline: Bosch Ltd Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR58,419 million and EBITDA rose 28% to INR8,180 million, with EBITDA margin near 14%.

Reported PAT of INR7,018 million fell 37.1% YoY because the prior year included an exceptional gain on sale of video solutions and access/intrusion businesses; excluding it, PAT grew 9.9%. Management said the Chassis Systems acquisition was completed in July and consolidation starts this quarter.

segments.name: Mobility Aftermarket

segments.name: 2-wheeler and Powersports

500550|2026-03.headline: Siemens Ltd Q4 FY26 (March quarter): orders up 33% to ₹67.3bn and revenue up 14.6% to ₹46.2bn, but EBITDA margin fell 290bp to 9.7% on commodity and FX costs.
500550|2026-03.overview: Management reported strong order intake and revenue growth in the March 2026 quarter, with all three businesses growing revenue double digits. Profitability was hit by material costs rising to 74% of revenue from 69% in Q2, driven by a roughly 18% Euro depreciation against INR and sharp rises in silver and copper. Backlog reached ₹450bn, up 9.3%, including a ₹18bn export bogie order executable over 2029-2039. Management gave no quarterly margin guidance and said two price increases have been taken in DI and SI, with a 3-4 month lag before they flow through.

segments.name: Digital Industries
segments.commentary: Q4 orders ₹9.7bn (+1.4% YoY, book-to-bill 0.84); revenue ₹11.5bn (+14.35%); EBITDA margin 2.6% vs 5% a year ago. 6M orders ₹20.7bn (+17.1%); management said margin ex-FX would be about 6.8%.

segments.name: Smart Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Q4 orders ₹29.6bn (+17.6%, book-to-bill 1.15); revenue ₹25.8bn (+14.5%). 6M orders ₹60.6bn (+22.9%), revenue +11.6%, EBITDA margin 15.1% vs 16.2% (down 120bp) on commodity costs. Volumes grew 17.5% in Q4 and 23% in 6M.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Q4 orders ₹28bn (+75%, book-to-bill 3.37) including the ₹18bn bogie export order; revenue ₹8.3bn (+12.7%) on 9K HP loco execution. Q4 EBIT margin 7.6% vs 7.2%; 6M EBITDA margin 6.4% vs 8.2%.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly margin guidance given; management said it cannot predict FX and commodity impact and will report it transparently.
Price increases: one taken before March and one after March, each with a 3-4 month lag; SI short-cycle LV products expected to return to aspired margin levels once price hikes stick.
Locomotive programme: 80 locos a year in FY26 and FY27, 100 a year in 2028-30, 160 a year in 2030-35; 40 delivered and paid by 31 March 2026, with 90%+ localisation.
Low-voltage motors business sale on track for completion in June 2026.
Management expects 0.5-1% GDP uplift over the next couple of years from the India-EU FTA; import costs in some segments to fall.
Locomotive margins are blended (O&M plus delivery) on percentage-of-completion; management said percentage margins on the next 80 locos should be similar, with absolute values scaling with volume.
capex_capacity: Medium-voltage and vacuum interrupter plant in Goa is nearing completion and should reach commercial production soon.
Mobility factories in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (bogies) and Nashik (propulsion and bogie electrics) under review for expansion, given the ₹18bn export order and pipeline; to be updated later.
Bogie order executes over 2029-2039 as product deliveries, not a project.
SI is 70-75% localised; DI localisation not viable at current volumes given PLC minimum volume needs; no capex quantum disclosed for the next 2-3 years.
demand_pricing: Management sees no slowdown in private or public capex; private capex pickup in cement, steel and pharma, with data centres and railways the key growth areas.

Q4 DI orders were flat because a price increase at the start of Q4 pulled orders into Q3; management said 6M growth of 17% is more representative.
Order backlog from data centres is about 12-15% excluding the bogie order (per management); data centre content sits mainly in SI.
Steel showed slight softness in the last 1-2 months; chemicals, pharma, food and beverage, cement and two-wheelers are growing.
Material costs rose to 74% of revenue in Q4 from 69% in Q2; silver up 160% and copper up 45% in USD terms between Q2 and Q4.
Cash flow weaker on inventory build due to West Asia crisis and higher receivables and contract assets in Mobility; management said overdues are stable.

qa_highlights.question: Will DI and SI margins hold at current levels for a few quarters, and will they improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no guidance; underlying margins are said to be strong, and DI and SI contracts are short-term with no long-term fixed prices, so impacts are short-term.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bogie order adequately protected against price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Wolfgang Wrumnig said the locomotive and bogie orders have price variation clauses with an index and the company is adequately covered, with some residual risk. Management would not disclose the value after adjustments.

qa_highlights.question: Why did DI orders decline YoY in Q4 and what is the domestic inflow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flat DI orders to a price increase at the start of Q4 that pulled orders into Q3. The CFO said the 6M DI growth of 17% is more representative, and railway orders should be read on a half-yearly basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that government ordering softens given fiscal pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no slowdown is visible in power utilities (mainly state government) or railways. The 24,000 km of signalling is already ordered, with the rest expected by end of next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and Nashik factories be expanded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is examining expansion for both factories given the backlog and pipeline and will update later. Metro rolling stock capacity decisions remain open.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 locomotive delivery impact on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 40 locos were delivered in Q4 only, and that revenue and margin recognition follows percentage-of-completion on cost inflow, not on the delivery count.

risks_watch: Commodity (copper, silver, aluminium) and EUR/INR volatility; the Euro moved from ₹91 to ₹107 per Euro between Q2 and Q6.
Pass-through lag and incomplete price pass-through in DI and SI, especially in negotiated medium-voltage and project business.
Working capital and cash conversion, with inventory and contract assets rising in Mobility.

Inflation and interest rate effects over the next 3-6 months on ordering.

500570|2026-03.headline: Tata Motors PV FY26 volumes hit a record 6.42 lakh units (+15% YoY); JLR full-year EBIT only 0.7%, with Rs 4,100 Cr of exceptionals.
500570|2026-03.overview: India PV business recovered strongly in H2 after a muted H1, with Q4 offtake above 2 lakh units (+37% YoY) and the company ranked number two on Vahan with over 14% share. Consolidated revenue for Q4 was about Rs 105,000 Cr (+7% YoY), with PBT before exceptionals of Rs 7,200 Cr, while full-year PBT of Rs 2,500 Cr excluded about Rs 4,100 Cr of exceptionals (cyber, labour code, demerger stamp duty). JLR delivered 95,000 Q4 wholesales and 9.2% EBIT, but full-year EBIT was 0.7% and management called the full-year performance far from intended. Management flagged commodity headwinds of 5-6% of revenue over 9-12 months and a Middle East demand hit in Q1, with guidance deferred to the June investor days.

segments.commentary: Q4 wholesales 95,000 and EBIT 9.2%, but FY26 EBIT of 0.7% and cash outflow of about GBP 2.2 billion, with two production quarters lost to the cyber incident. Defender grew YoY in Q4; Jaguar volumes fell 5,700 units as the brand transitions.

guidance_outlook: JLR targets GBP 1.7 billion of cost savings over two years, aiming to bring cash breakeven volume back toward 300,000 units a year; savings to start showing from H2 FY27.
India: management expects industry growth of about 10% in FY27, with high double-digit growth in H1 and moderation in H2; TMPV aims for industry-beating growth.

India: about 0.5% price increase taken in April 2026, with further measured price increases under consideration; commodity headwind estimated at 5-6% of revenue over 9-12 months (about 3.5-4% expected in Q4 FY26).
JLR financial guidance for FY27 to be given at the Investor Day on 17 June 2026; India Analyst Day on 23 June 2026.
EV production to rise beyond 10,000 units a month from May 2026; Sierra.ev launch expected next quarter.
capex_capacity: India FY26 capex about Rs 4,300 Cr (7.5% of revenue), within guided range for combined PV and EV capex.
Sierra supply constrained by casting suppliers on the new engine; immediate milestone is to cross 10,000 units a month with additional suppliers added.
EV run rate about 24,000 a quarter on average and about 27,000 in Q4, with a monthly run rate of about 9,000; production to rise by about 10% from May.
JLR investment is largely in UK plant facilities for three new architectures and BEV powertrains at the Wolverhampton propulsion facility.
Dealer inventory in India about 20 days; waiting periods 4-8 weeks, longer for Sierra and certain EVs.
demand_pricing: India industry FY26 volumes hit a record 4.7 million units (+8%); H2 grew 17% post GST 2.0, and April-May demand momentum stayed at a high level.
Nexon and Punch ranked number one and number three models in the industry during H2 FY26.
EV bookings up roughly 25-30% after the Middle East crisis began in February, though supply, not demand, is the constraint.

JLR ASPs fell marginally QoQ to about GBP 72,000 from GBP 76,000, mainly due to sterling strength against the dollar ($1.36 Q4 average vs $1.325 in Q3). Q4 gross margin fell on higher VME (7% vs 5% last year) and warranty charges.
JLR China volumes fell 27% YoY in FY26 due to luxury tax and dealer-stock reduction; US retailer stock brought down after tariffs, now slightly below normal levels.
Middle East (6% of JLR sales mix) expected to be hit in Q1 FY27; Middle East dealers are running out of stock.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the commodity headwind, and how will it be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated the impact at 5-6% of revenue over 9-12 months, with about 2% offset by cost reductions in FY26 and 0.5% price increase taken in April. Further measured price increases are under consideration but not decided.

qa_highlights.question: Will EV volumes step up, and will net pricing improve?
qa_highlights.answer: EV run rate is about 9,000 a month and expected to rise above 10,000 from May; demand is strong but supply constrained. Long-term EV cost trends are deflationary versus inflationary ICE costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Range Rover EV launch timing and pre-bookings?
qa_highlights.answer: Range Rover Electric is coming soon as the first JLR EV launch, with three reveals in H2 CY26. There are no firm pre-bookings, but about 78,000 expressions of interest.

qa_highlights.question: How are geopolitics and fuel prices affecting EV demand and investment plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Middle East war does not change launch timelines or investment plans, but JLR will need to keep ICE, PHEV, MHEV and BEV offerings in parallel for longer than planned.

qa_highlights.question: How is JLR planning to reduce its breakeven volume to 300,000?
qa_highlights.answer: The GBP 1.7 billion plan covers end-to-end procurement (now a separate Board-level vertical), warranty cost reduction and IT/digital productivity; benefits to start from H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 industry growth and TMPV's supply situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth expected at about 10%, with high double-digit H1. Management said FY27 is a supply challenge rather than demand, with two new nameplates and four facelifts each for ICE and EV planned.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a prior-period item in Q4 PLI accrual?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, about Rs 90 Cr related to Q3 that was certified in Q4; excluding it, Q4 PLI would be about Rs 380 Cr against Rs 471 Cr reported.

Sierra and EV supply ramp is dependent on casting suppliers and new capacity; EV volumes are constrained despite strong demand.
JLR warranty cost increases (notably the US) and rising VME (7% vs 5%) continue to pressure margins.
Sterling strength against the dollar and tariffs weigh on JLR cash flow; FY26 cash flow was impacted by lower payables.
China luxury tax and the Chinese OEM push in Europe and the UK pose competitive risks for JLR.

The issue is supply. It will completely depend on ramping up, how fast we are able to ramp up the volumes.
So, given this new world order in supply and demand side of our business, what's our response?
Demand for the moment is slightly a secondary concern.

rows.why: Sierra.ev launch is expected next quarter, Range Rover Electric has about 78,000 expressions of interest with three reveals in H2 CY26, and FY27 includes two new nameplates and four facelifts each for ICE and EV.

rows.why: Exports were 10,000+ in FY26 and management is targeting 70% to 100% growth in FY27.

rows.why: Management targets GBP 1.7 bn of savings over two years, from a FY26 JLR wholesale base of 308,000 units, with benefits starting H2 FY27.

500570|2026-06.headline: TMPV Q1 FY27: India volumes up 46% to 182,000 units, but 4.5% commodity hit held India EBITDA at about 4%; JLR PBT fell to GBP 109 million.
500570|2026-06.overview: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (formerly Tata Motors) posted Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 95,800 Cr, EBIT margin of 2.4% and PBT of Rs 1,600 Cr, down year on year. JLR wholesales fell about 10% (around 8,000 units) on Jaguar run-out, a supplier fire at Solihull and Middle East disruption, with JLR PBT at GBP 109 million versus GBP 351 million last year. India wholesales rose 46% to about 182,000 units and share rose 200 bps to 14.3%, but a 4.5% commodity hit in Q1 offset fixed-cost leverage and material savings, holding EBITDA margin at about 4%. Management says FY27 guidance for JLR is not changed.

segments.name: India PV (TMPV domestic)
segments.commentary: Wholesales about 182,000 units, up 46% YoY vs industry +24%; market share 14.3%, up 200 bps; firm #2 on registrations. EV volumes over 34,000 units (about 20% of sales), with July EV volume above 15,000 and EV share 43%.

segments.name: JLR
segments.commentary: Wholesales down about 10% YoY (about 8,000 units, around 3,000 below internal plan). Defender up YoY; Range Rover and Range Rover Sport hit by a chassis supplier fire early in the quarter. Retail down 14.5K YoY, with over 5,000 from Jaguar run-out and Middle East. China wholesales down 25%.

guidance_outlook: JLR FY27 guidance not changed; management says Q1 is not inconsistent with full-year guidance but needs strong rest-of-year performance.
TMPV targets higher double-digit volume growth in FY27 and 10% revenue growth per annum at group level.
Group targets $1.7 billion of cost savings across ex-works cost, warranty and fixed costs; detail promised with Q2 results.

India: Q2 commodity hit of about 3% expected; margins expected flattish vs Q1 after 0.5% July price increase, accelerated cost reduction (1.5% in Q1) and 1% IPL benefit; margin step-up expected in H2 as PLI accrues from Q3.
JLR expects about 12,000 EVs in FY27 (tentative); Type 01 and Range Rover GT impact mainly FY28.
India exports targeted at about 2x FY26 levels in FY27.
Avinya launch slips into 2027 due to platform change to JLR's Freelander platform.
capex_capacity: India Q1 capex Rs 1,300 Cr; to step up as next growth phase executes per Investor Day guidance.
JLR capitalisation rate 74%; spend over balance of year similar, shifting from engineering to capital as new facilities come online and four BEVs enter series production.

demand_pricing: India volumes run-rate has consistently exceeded 60,000 a month vs earlier 45,000-50,000; EV mix 19% in Q1, 23% exit June, 24% in July.

India price increases total 1% (0.5% in April and 0.5% in July); commodity impact 4.5% in Q1 and about 3% expected in Q2; management says further calibrated increases and accelerated cost cuts will follow.
Dealer inventory about 30 days; management wants a significant build ahead of festive season and October retail.
EV bookings about 3.5x pre-Middle East crisis (Jan-Feb) levels; supply far below demand.
JLR China wholesales down 25%; management expects China to get worse before stabilising, citing retrospective taxes and luxury tax changes.
JLR VME (variable marketing expense) rose to 7.1%; JLR average transaction price trending up, targeting above GBP 80,000 per car in about 18 months.
JLR aluminium fell from about $3,500/t end-March to about $3,150/t end-June; some contracts reset quarterly, so Q2 may see extra raw material hit.
Industry PV volumes exceeded 1.3 million units, up 24% YoY; industry growth expected to moderate in H2 on higher base.

qa_highlights.question: Are JLR's Q1 temporary issues behind us and what is the volume recovery and Type 01 ramp plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Jaguar wholesales of about 1,500 units lower QoQ are being run out over 3-6 months; Type 01 production starts early next year with impact in FY28, not FY27. The Solihull supplier fire is fully resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why only 1% price increase despite strong raw material headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is benchmarked against competitors to protect competitiveness; more frequent, progressive increases will follow as cost reductions allow, avoiding a steep single hike.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume and margin outlook for India?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting higher double-digit volume growth in FY27; margins to be neutralised through a mix of price increases and cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Will JLR localise production in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Not localising existing models given volume scale; MoU with Stellantis for new US-specific vehicles (Defender brand), with a definitive agreement targeted by year end.

qa_highlights.question: How does rising EV mix affect JLR margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects BEV Range Rover models to be at least margin neutral and not discounted; the EMA cars replace low-margin models so should be neutral to accretive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sierra supply outlook for the festive season?
qa_highlights.answer: Engine casting and sheet-metal constraints are easing over the next two months, with major capacity additions from October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 margin outlook after the 3% commodity hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Net of price increase, cost reduction and the absence of Q1's 1% IPL seasonal impact, Q2 margins are expected to be flattish vs Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What JLR EV volume is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Tentatively about 12,000 EVs in FY27, starting with Range Rover Electric production in September.

risks_watch: JLR free cash flow deeply negative (about GBP 1 billion after working capital in Q1); working capital expected to reverse through the year.
China: retailer stress and new luxury taxes; management expects further deterioration before stabilising.
Commodity inflation: about 3% further hit in Q2 from quarterly contract resets; PLI certification for most models only from Q3-Q4.
Credit ratings: JLR at the edge of investment grade with negative watch; debt at GBP 3.6 billion.
Middle East disruption and Strait of Hormuz routing affecting retail and wholesale; Q1 MENA retail down about 1,400 units.
Supply constraints at Sierra and Punch.ev; India dealer stock at about 30 days.
