500575|2026-03.headline: Voltas Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT fell to INR 181 crores from INR 343 crores as UCP margins were hit by commodity inflation and rupee depreciation.
500575|2026-03.overview: Consolidated total income rose marginally to INR 4,930 crores in Q4 FY26 from INR 4,847 crores, but PBT fell to INR 181 crores and net profit to INR 113 crores from INR 343 crores and INR 236 crores. For FY26, total income fell to INR 14,483 crores from INR 15,737 crores, PBT to INR 557 crores from INR 1,191 crores, and net profit to INR 377 crores from INR 834 crores. Management said March 2026 was a record sales month and April was close to that level, but margins were compressed by old-cost inventory, FX losses and commodity inflation, with price hikes only partly passed through so far.

segments.name: Segment A - UCP (RAC, CAC, CR, AR, Voltbek)
segments.commentary: FY26 RAC volume was 2.25 million units; Voltas leads the No. 2 player by a 5.1% primary market share gap. Margins were hit in Q1-Q2 by channel overhang and in Q4 by commodity inflation and rupee depreciation. Chennai plant utilisation is ~1.2 lakh units/month against 1.5 million units annual capacity.

segments.name: Voltbek (within Segment A)
segments.commentary: Year-to-date market share of 8.6% in washing machines and 6.2% in refrigerators in a sluggish market. Sanand plant localisation is ongoing and management expects margin expansion over the medium term.

segments.name: Segment B - Electro-Mechanical Projects (MEP)
segments.commentary: Order book close to INR 6,200 crores at 31 March 2026, of which ~INR 4,500 crores is domestic. Management says 40-50% of the India MEP book and some international contracts carry price variation clauses, so commodity and labour inflation is passed through. No client has invoked force majeure; Qatar force majeure was revoked.

segments.name: Segment C - Mining, Construction & Textile Machinery
segments.commentary: Mining and construction equipment showed steady top-line growth, supported by crushing and screening demand and Mozambique operations. Textile machinery was weak amid cautious capex sentiment, with management pinning hopes on Union Budget 2026 and PLI support for spinning recovery.

guidance_outlook: UCP margins: management said the target is a gradual step-up towards FY25 levels (UCP margin ~8.4% in FY25 vs ~3.2% in FY26, per analyst); no firm FY27 margin number given, and no timeline for returning to FY25 levels.
Q4 FY26 margins: management said it is not expecting any sharp downturn in margin profile for the quarter (Q1 FY27), with costs hitting progressively as a mix of pre-war and post-war costs.

Pricing: further price increases are planned, depending on rupee-dollar, war and commodity moves; management said it is watching prices almost weekly and sees double-digit inflation, to be passed through as costs hit. Pass-through expected for most brands.

Demand: industry RAC expected to grow at least 15-20% in FY27 off a weak FY26 base (industry FY26 degrowth ~10-12%, 14.3 million primary units); commercial refrigeration expected to grow upwards of 10%; commercial AC expected to grow 12-15%.
Medium-term: Voltbek expected to steadily improve brand preference, penetration and operating leverage over the medium term; management expects margin expansion at Sanand over time.

Capacity and capex: small capex to lift Chennai from 1.5 million to 2 million units is ready; third investment round deferred 1-2 years until demand is visible. Capex focus remains on Segment A (capacity, R&D, CAC).
capex_capacity: Chennai plant built to 1.5 million units capacity (up from 1 million last year), running at about 1.2 lakh units per month; a small capex to take it to 2 million units is ready, with the third investment round deferred 1-2 years until demand is visible.
Pantnagar and Chennai facilities running at higher utilisation than last year.
Ongoing capex in factory automation, warehouse rationalisation and integrated inventory planning.
Capex is mostly directed at Segment A (capacity and R&D); CAC is a key area for capex deployment.
Sanand plant localisation and scale-up for Voltbek is in progress.
demand_pricing: Price hikes: new BEE table products (from March) carried 5% on 3-star (~75% mix) and 10% on 5-star (~25% mix), a blended ~6-7%, plus a further 1-2% (copper) and another increase in the latest month, linked to rupee depreciation.
GST on RAC cut from 28% to 18% cushions consumer affordability this summer versus last year.
Channel inventory is under 45 days and closer to 30 days, per management.
March 2026 was a record sales month in company history; April was close to that level and May is tracking well. Secondary sales are picking up as the higher-priced stock is absorbed.
Competition: about 60 brands in RAC; management said the company holds a 5.1% primary share lead over the next cluster of four brands.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins for UCP be modelled for FY27 and FY28, given UCP margin of ~3.2% in FY26 against 8.4% in FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1-Q2 margins were hit by a channel stock overhang from erratic summer and early monsoon, and that some pressures are structural (supply chain, currency). The aim is gradual improvement towards FY25 levels, through pricing and cost actions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall only ~85 bps while segment margins fell sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: No direct reconciliation was given. Management pointed to the Q1-Q2 overhang and later commodity and FX pressures as the drivers of the segment drop.

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the ~INR 55 crore FX loss in H2, how much hit Q4, and how much extra marketing was spent?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 still used the mix of old and new inventory: old stock was consumed in the first 4-6 weeks of the quarter. Marketing was managed within the existing pool and was broadly comparable, with brand ambassador costs the only extra item. The FX share in Q4 was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Will cost inflation hit Q1 margins and could they dip significantly before price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs will hit progressively, a mix of pre-war and post-war costs. Management expects no sharp margin downturn in the quarter, with more price actions to follow. Unallocated costs rose on forex and treasury mark-to-market.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify price actions and provide RAC volume and the MEP domestic/international order book split?
qa_highlights.answer: Price actions are detailed above. FY26 RAC volume was 2.25 million units. The order book is ~INR 6,200 crores, of which ~INR 4,500 crores is domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company seen force majeure or margin risk in the MEP business from metal price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: No client has invoked force majeure; Qatar's temporary contractor option was revoked. Price variation clauses cover 40-50% of the India MEP book and some international contracts, so margin risk is limited.

qa_highlights.question: What is channel inventory and Chennai utilisation, and what is the domestic share of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel inventory is under 45 days, closer to 30. Chennai runs at ~1.2 lakh units per month against 1.5 million units annual capacity. The domestic order book is ~INR 4,500 crores.

Margin recovery depends on pricing pass-through and on the old-cost inventory running out; Q1 FY27 margins are the first test.
Unallocated costs, including forex and treasury mark-to-market, rose sharply in Q4 and need to be tracked.

Inventory was moderately elevated at Q4 end and is expected to normalise as seasonal demand builds.

500575|2026-06.headline: Voltas Q1 FY27 net profit rose to Rs 213 crore (Rs 141 crore) on revenue of Rs 4,765 crore, with RAC market share at 17.3%.
500575|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income grew to Rs 4,765 crore from Rs 4,021 crore, with PBT of Rs 285 crore versus Rs 203 crore. Segment A (unitary cooling) grew 33%, with RAC volumes up 45% and secondary market share at 17.3% against 15.9% for FY26, widening the lead over the nearest competitor to 4 percentage points. Commodity inflation, rupee depreciation and freight costs were largely passed on (10-12% cost increase, near full pass-through), and UCP EBIT margin improved to 5.3% from 3.7%. Projects (Segment B) was soft on execution issues and delayed new orders in the Middle East, while Commercial Refrigeration and Air Coolers were muted. Management also signed a binding term sheet for a 50-50 compressor JV with Atomberg.

segments.name: Segment A - Unitary Cooling Products (RAC, Commercial AC, Commercial Refrigeration, Air Coolers, Voltbek)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 33% led by RAC; secondary RAC share 17.3% (FY26: 15.9%). Commercial AC stable; Commercial Refrigeration and Air Coolers muted, with industry degrowth around 15% in commercial refrigeration per management. Voltbek posted record quarterly sales, with YTD share of 9.4% in washing machines and 7.4% in refrigerators; still loss-making.

segments.name: Segment B - Electromechanical Projects and Services
segments.commentary: Domestic order momentum strong (industrial infrastructure, electronics, metro/tunnel, data centres), but top line soft due to execution challenges. International new orders delayed by Middle East conflict; Sidra Bank guarantees of QAR 167 million (about Rs 433 crore) cancelled after court award.

segments.name: Segment C - Engineering Products and Services
segments.commentary: High double-digit top-line growth; Mining and Construction Equipment grew strongly on crushing and screening demand and O&M contracts. Textile Machinery grew double digits with early signs of order-book revival.

guidance_outlook: Voltbek EBITDA breakeven, previously targeted for FY27, likely pushed out by a few quarters due to commodity inflation.
UCP margin aspiration of 7%+ (management cited prior quarters above 7%), with improvement targeted year-on-year over the next ~8 quarters; no firm timeline given.
Electromechanical projects: Q2 may not be much better; recovery expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Q2 expected to be seasonally leaner for cooling; channel inventory maintained at around 4 weeks.
No price increase planned unless West Asia-driven costs rise further; any margin upside to come via lower channel schemes.
Projects strategy shifting to shorter-gestation private-sector, data centre, manufacturing and MEP jobs; fewer government projects with payment-delay risk.
capex_capacity: Atomberg 50-50 JV for RAC compressors: planned capacity about 2.8 million units; ramp from under 1 million, to 1-2 million, then 2.5+ million; commercial production about 18 months from start of work.
Total JV capex not yet quantified; expected to be split 50-50, with majority spend in FY28-FY29 per CFO's assumption.
No major capex planned for FY27-FY28 beyond maintenance; Chennai capacity already built. Chennai (~1.5 million units) and Pantnagar (~1.4 million units) plants at high utilisation.
Outsourcing share stable: Window ACs ~100% OEM (about 10% of peak-quarter AC sales); Split ACs about 75% self-manufactured and 25% OEM.
demand_pricing: Industry RAC secondary sales up about 15% (GfK Nielsen); management estimates primary growth of 20-22% in volume and 25-26% in value.

Cost inflation of 10-12% in FY27 peak: about 7-8% from BEE table change (3-star +5%, 5-star +15%), plus 4-5% from commodities, rupee depreciation, freight and plastics; near-full pass-through achieved.
Commercial Refrigeration costs rose about 10% for freezers, 15% for water coolers and 10% for water dispensers; channel resisted, with traction improving this quarter.
Peer RAC players' EBIT reportedly fell 3-4 percentage points; Voltas says its Q1-on-Q1 EBIT margin improved.
Channel cautious on stock; July-August demand not yet clear, festive season view too early.

qa_highlights.question: Compressor JV: capacity, capex, timeline and split among the three entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity about 2.8 million compressors; total capex still early-stage. Commercial production about 18 months away; the JV was driven by supply security and QCO import limits.

qa_highlights.question: Voltbek EBITDA breakeven timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier target for this year; West Asia-driven commodity spike meant brands could not pass through all costs, so breakeven may slip by a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How do QCO norms get met until the JV is operational?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports allowed up to 30% based on FY25 volumes; continued purchases from Highly and GMCC (India capacity blocked), blending with own supply later.

qa_highlights.question: Why UCP margins are 5% in a strong quarter, and what is steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peers saw EBIT fall 3-4 pts; Voltas improved YoY on scale, no factory disruption, cost absorption and cost-out. Aspiration of 7%+ over the next ~8 quarters; CFO said margins vary quarter to quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Projects margin outlook and order book quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Calibrated order booking to avoid fixed-price contracts without escalation clauses; shifting to shorter-gestation private, data-centre and MEP jobs.

qa_highlights.question: Channel inventory and July-August demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel cautious; inventory around 4 weeks; too early to judge festive season, with a 4-6 week monitoring window.

qa_highlights.question: Voltbek loss in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Share of JV loss booked at Rs 37 crore; EMP margins to improve in Q3-Q4 after a soft Q2.

500620|2026-03.headline: GE Shipping posts best-ever quarterly profit and first-ever INR1,000 crore annual consolidated net profit, with INR35.10 full-year dividend per share.
500620|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as the best-ever quarter for profit and FY26 as the best-ever year on consolidated profit, crossing INR1,000 crore net profit for the first time, partly helped by FX movement. Standalone NAV rose to about INR1,422 per share from just over INR1,100 a year earlier, and the company declared its highest-ever quarterly dividend of INR11.70 per share. The Strait of Hormuz closure tightened crude, product and LPG markets in March and April, with spot rates spiking and settling at still-high levels. Management declined to give earnings or quarter-ahead outlook, citing a largely spot-exposed fleet.

Jack-up day rates in Nigeria described as firm; Indian short-term rig rates described as reasonably remunerative but not high.
ONGC rig employment has fallen to one of its lowest levels; an active ONGC tender is ongoing with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: How are day rates trending versus last quarter across tankers and dry bulk?

500620|2026-06.headline: GE Shipping posted record Q1 FY27 consolidated profit of INR 1,309 crore (standalone INR 1,157 crore), with ~INR 91-92/share EPS and a INR 14.40 interim dividend.

Standalone NAV rose about INR 100/share to ~INR 1,512 and consolidated NAV is just under INR 1,900/share, with the stock trading at about a 25% discount. The company announced its 18th consecutive interim dividend of INR 14.40/share, its highest quarterly payout. Management said it remains predominantly on the spot market (about 25-26% of capacity on time charter), is net cash, and is holding most cash rather than buying ships at peak prices.

financial_highlights.change: Most profitable quarter ever, per management

financial_highlights.value: ~USD 700 million gross, ~USD 600 million net of debt

segments.name: Product tankers (MR/LR2)
segments.commentary: MR spot earnings were close to $50,000/day in the last quarter. Product tanker TC coverage is about $45,000/day; product rates are significantly lower than in Q1. Some LR2s switched to dirty Aframax trades because of the earnings gap.

segments.name: LPG (VLGC)
segments.commentary: Fleet is on fixed-rate time charters. One vessel has profit-sharing upside. Repricing of one time charter came in 25-30% above the prior charter rate; another VLGC comes off charter in Q1 CY2027 at about $15,000-20,000/day above its current rate.

segments.name: Dry bulk
segments.commentary: Bulk earnings were marginally better than a year ago. Coal demand rose as LNG disruption pushed power plants to coal, and grain trade was strong. Bulk carrier rates are marginally higher than in Q1.

500645|2026-06.headline: Deepak Fertilisers Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA hit record INR845 crore (+65% YoY) at 26% margin; PAT INR490 crore (+101% YoY).

Margin expanded to 26% from 19% a year ago and about 12% in Q4 FY26, driven by stronger TAN, nitric acid and IPA realisations plus early benefits of Equinor LNG supply, which began with the first cargo in May. Net debt fell to INR4,719 crore and debt/EBITDA improved to 1.4x despite over INR500 crore of quarterly capex. 500650|2026-03.headline: Excel Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR281 crore, while FY26 revenue grew 11.8% to INR1,094 crore with adjusted EBITDA of INR112 crore (10.1% margin).

500655|2026-06.headline: Garware Hi-Tech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR633 crore and EBITDA margin hit a record 30.30%, with FY27 guidance reaffirmed.

Management attributed the margin to product mix (Sun Control and high-IR products, architectural share) rather than one-offs, and said Q3 will be seasonally lower. Tariff refunds were excluded from Q1 and about 30-40% had been received by the call date, with the balance expected in Q2. FY27 guidance of over INR2,500 crore revenue and 25% plus/minus 2% EBITDA margin was reaffirmed; management also flagged Middle East shipping disruption that delayed some Q1 volume into Q2.

segments.name: Paint Protection Film (PPF)
segments.commentary: About 20% of Q1 revenue versus about 25% last year. Old PPF line runs near 100%; new line at about 60%. Some volume slipped to Q2 due to a ship stuck at Jebel Ali. Five OEM relationships including M&M.

segments.name: Architectural films
segments.commentary: Management says architectural now exceeds 25% of revenue (vs about 5% earlier, as stated) and is the highest-margin product set on like-for-like basis, per management.

segments.name: Garware Home Solutions (D2C)
segments.commentary: 9 studios operational, target 50 by end FY27. 100% direct-to-consumer; Q1 sales described as very small with no figure given. Management said D2C could exceed INR100 crore.

financial_highlights.change: -2% YoY; base included ~INR 330 crore one-off tax credit
Stepped up sequentially; highest in 11 quarters

segments.commentary: USG 14% on high-single-digit UVG, the strongest in 3 years. Fabric Wash grew double digits, volume-led; Household Care (Vim Liquid) grew double digits in USG and UVG. Calibrated price increases taken on crude-linked inputs.

segments.commentary: USG 12% on high-single-digit UVG. Hair Care grew double digits, volume-led; Skin Care and Colour Cosmetics grew high single digit, with Premium Skin Care at double digit and Minimalist accelerating. Health & Wellbeing (OZiva) was soft as the business transitions toward emerging demand spaces.

segments.commentary: USG 4%, driven by price increases taken for palm oil inflation for a second year. Skin Cleansing grew mid single digit (Dove and Pears premium bars double digit; Bodywash double digit); soaps volumes declined mid-single digit per analyst question. Oral Care grew mid single digit.

Capital Markets Day scheduled for September 2026 for strategy update.

Unilever Fragrance House launched in India as part of a global fragrance capability programme.
Digital-first distribution centre in Vijayawada with AI-enabled real-time visibility.

Rural and urban both growing robustly; mass and premium both competitive, with premiumization in line with market trend.
Tea early-season read shows inflationary trend; pricing decisions to follow buying season.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the mid-single-digit soaps volume decline, and what is market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to palm oil inflation over two years; it is focusing on premiumization (Dove, Pears double digit, Bodywash double digit) and does not disclose segment share, saying it is winning turnover-weighted share overall.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said A&P is at its highest in 11-12 quarters, with better ROI from AI-enabled programmes and media procurement savings, so like-for-like comparisons are not strictly valid.

qa_highlights.question: Is the El Nino and monsoon risk material to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a difficult versus good agriculture year moves GDP by 50-60 bps; MSP hikes of 5-6% insulate rural income, and a rainfall deficit of about 15% is seen as not meaningfully impacting the economy.

qa_highlights.question: At what crude level can 23% margin be held without further price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a precise crude threshold, but said it can maintain margins with about half of inflation passed through and that crude of $75-100/bbl is manageable; $140-160 would be a different discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quick commerce slowdown affecting HUL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QCom grew 40-50% and the channel remains structurally attractive, with new entrants and tailored assortments and pack architecture.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (palm oil, crude-linked derivatives, tea) and the pace of calibrated pricing needed to hold 23% EBITDA margin.
Soaps volume decline under palm oil-led price pressure and value competition in soaps and liquids.
Monsoon progression (rainfall deficit cited at about 15%) and El Nino impact on rural demand.
OZiva growth moderation in Health & Wellbeing and the stated transition of the business.
Management's shift from prior quarter's language on navigating volatility to cautioning on monsoon and geopolitics; watch wording at the September Capital Markets Day.

we remain confident that FY '27 will be better than FY'26.

the barriers to entry may have got reduced, Priya, what you keep saying, but the barrier to scale has only gone up

tone.note: Management was confident on Q1 growth (10% USG, highest in 13 quarters) and FY27 being better than FY26, but cautious on monsoon, crude and geopolitics, and declined crude thresholds, soaps share and segment guidance; analysts pressed on margin defence against ~10% cost inflation versus ~5% pricing

500710|2026-03.headline: JSW Dulux Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6.2% on 23% blended volume growth, with price and mix cuts holding back realisations and EBITDA margin near 14.4%.
500710|2026-03.overview: Management reported a record 23% blended volume growth across decorative and industrial paints, with revenue up 6.2%, the gap driven mainly by price and mix after premium price corrections from September-October 2025. Like-for-like EBITDA grew about 2% and PBT declined slightly, while the EBITDA margin was stated at around 14.4%. Management said raw material inflation since March 2026 has forced a price increase of about 9.7% through mid-May, with an estimated further 3-4% needed. The company also booked INR64.8 crore from the final real estate sale and proposed a final dividend of INR50 per share.

financial_highlights.change: Record, per management; decorative and industrial both grew strongly
YoY; one of strongest in last 4 quarters
Largely protected vs prior year per CFO
Last of real estate sale, completed March 2026

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Very strong volume growth amid competition; premium growth good, retail and semi-urban grew faster; Dulux Velvet Touch luxury finishes launched; mass and economy push increasing. Decorative is about 20% direct (projects) and 80% distributor-led, with roughly 75% of total via distributors.

segments.name: Industrial (Automotive & Specialty, Marine & Protective, Coil)
segments.commentary: Growth across all three verticals; mid-market automotive refinish under pressure; Porsche refinish tie-up announced; marine and protective had one of its highest revenue months in March; coil won marquee projects including Navi Mumbai Airport. Industrial capacity utilisation cited at 70-80%.

guidance_outlook: Management targets double-digit volume growth going forward, with the gap between volume and revenue expected to narrow over a couple of quarters.
Further price increase of about 3-4% needed industry-wide to offset RMC inflation of 24-25% (raw materials about 55% of RMC; implied about 13.5% need), per management estimate.
Price correction drag of about 1.5-2% expected to continue into the coming quarter; mix and price effects expected to neutralise by August-September.
FY27 margins may compress for about a quarter if elevated crude and raw material levels persist, though management sees no structural issue.
Integrated SAP and systems work planned around post-Diwali, towards end of calendar 2026; Mumbai HQ shift ongoing.
Dealer integration: projects business integrated; combined JSW Dulux and JSW Paints sales teams in 7 metros from later in May; retail integration only planned for early FY28 (early calendar 2027).
capex_capacity: Current decorative paint capacity utilisation stated at 55-60%.
Industrial capacity utilisation stated at up to 70-80% after additional capacity was added.

Cross-manufacturing being piloted: JSW Paints (earlier made only at Vijayanagar) to be made across plants; some southern-state products to move from Hyderabad and Thane to Vijayanagar; first trial batches produced.
Management said capex will be invested in capacity expansion and localisation; no specific amount or timeline disclosed.
demand_pricing: Blended volume growth of 23% partly reflected dealer pre-buying ahead of price increases, estimated at a week to 10 days; management said offtake tracked in line with sell-in.
Price increases of about 9.7% taken through mid-May 2026 (gross, before price-correction adjustments).
Premium contribution in Dulux at mid-40s percent vs about 22% for the industry; management said premium price premiums were cut from 7-9% and mid-market is now almost at parity with Berger.
Competition described as very intense; some competitors operating higher discounts; industry aggression expected for coming quarters.
Dealer and channel pushback after strategic review announcement in 2025 (warranty concerns) said to be behind the company.
Management aims to become a strong number 3 in decorative from number 4 (blended 8% market share target referenced; decorative progress described as a longer journey).

qa_highlights.question: Is cultural, dealer and systems integration complete, and has it hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Culture integration early but going well; HQ moved to Mumbai. Only projects dealer integration done; retail integration planned for early next year. HR integrated. SAP integration planned around post-Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company over-indexed on premium pricing and at parity with Berger?
qa_highlights.answer: Some premium brands still carry about 2% desired premium; mid-market almost at par with Berger, though some competitors discount more.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 23% volume growth driven by channel fill or pre-buying, and what is FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth is blended and secular; some dealer pre-buy in March; offtake similar. Management targets double-digit volume growth over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective price hike after price cuts and trade spend changes?
qa_highlights.answer: The 9.7% increase is gross; price correction impact of about 1.5-2% in the quarter continues into next quarter, to be absorbed by the price increase.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative utilisation 55-60%, industrial up to 70-80%; cross-manufacturing underway; capacity expansion and localisation on the agenda, no figures given.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 outlook given oil and war-related uncertainty?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is scenario planning; elevated levels could compress margins for about a quarter, but structural demand is intact.

risks_watch: Raw material and crude-linked cost inflation (RMC inflation 24-25%); further pricing needed; margin compression risk for about a quarter.
Price correction and mix drag of 1.5-2% over the next quarter; volume-revenue gap to narrow.
Intense competition and discounting from peers; possible dealer destocking as price cuts and inventory levels differ across players.
Integration risk: retail dealer integration deferred; SAP and systems migration around end-2026.
Whether Q4 volume partly reflected March pre-buying, so Q1 FY27 sell-in may soften.
Auto OEM entry and decorative market-share gains still unproven; management timeline is towards the last quarter of FY27.

rows.why: Coil division won marquee projects including Navi Mumbai Airport and marine/protective had one of its highest revenue months in March, though no order value was disclosed.

500710|2026-06.headline: JSW Dulux Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.8% to ₹965 crore on ~25% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% with PAT lifted by one-offs.
500710|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 18.8% like-to-like to ₹965 crore, with volume up about 25% (about 18-19% after price). Gross margin was 37.4%, which management says was depressed by roughly 2 points of high-cost inventory and about 2.5 points from reclassifying promotional spends to gross revenue; underlying gross margin was put at 39.5-40%. EBITDA rose 14.7% to ₹115.1 crore but margin diluted about 50 bps to 11.9% after headcount additions (~160 people) and R&D investment. Reported PAT of ₹135.5 crore includes one-offs: ₹55.9 crore dividend from ICICI R&T and ₹108 crore income tax refund (incl. ₹21.5 crore interest) for AY 2013-14.

financial_highlights.change: Management: underlying ~39.5-40% before inventory and reclassification effects
Other income; linked to real estate monetisation

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Grew double digits (management cites ~20% volume growth) and is ~60% of business; premium is ~45% of decorative and led growth, with premium and luxury growing high double digits. Mass and economy grew lower.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: All sub-segments grew upwards of 25%; automotive grew strongly with premium OEM and refinish wins (Porsche, Mahindra, MG via JSW group, Sikkens body shops).

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected in 13-15% range going forward, as reinvestment costs normalise and input prices ease.
Management expects Q2 growth in a similar band to Q1 despite a weaker July due to late rains; target is double-digit volume and value growth.
Strategic ambition: become number two in decorative and number one in industrial coatings, with a 2030-31 vision; decorative aim is market share gains while protecting absolute EBITDA.
Project Akshaya cost programme targets synergies with JSW Paints; ₹2.4 crore savings realised in Q1 and a 3-year roadmap set.
ERP migration from AkzoNobel systems planned by end of calendar year; TSA period is limited.
capex_capacity: Active towns about 3,400-3,500 out of 5,000+ presence; target to lift to about 4,500 this year, focusing on towns above 20,000 population.
Shift to direct/hybrid model in about the top 20 high-share towns; distributor model retained elsewhere.
Cross-manufacturing: JSW Paints made at Gwalior; JSW Dulux products made in JSW Paints plants; some JSW Paints products made in Mohali.
Headquarters moved from Delhi to JSW Centre, Mumbai during Q1.
demand_pricing: Volume growth ~25%, with price contributing ~6-7 points; growth driven by value per outlet from existing outlets, broadly secular across outlet types.
Gross-to-net reclassification of promotional spends (~2.5% of blended revenue) reduced reported gross margin; management says this aligns with industry presentation.
Management says decorative pricing has stabilised but competition from new entrants, with discounting, will persist for 1-2 years.

Discount ratio includes distributor commission (~4.5-4.7% of revenue), which management says makes dealer commissions otherwise modest; company benchmarks pricing to the market leader, not new entrants.
Benefit expected as high-priced inventory bought at end-March is consumed; lower-cost stock now entering August.

qa_highlights.question: What execution changes are driving better decorative performance, beyond headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-market segmentation by share tiers; reinforced Velvet Touch and WeatherShield; focus on undercoats such as primers in weak states; digital lead management, AI/analytics and an architect/painter programme. Hybrid direct model being tested in top 20 towns.

qa_highlights.question: How does volume-value gap reconcile with mix improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three factors: high-cost inventory, ~2.5% gross-to-net reclassification, and faster growth in lower-margin industrial and other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Target for top-three position and inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined JSW Paints and JSW Dulux revenue is about ₹6,000 crore. Aim is to become number two; industrial to be number one in 1-1.5 years and wider ambition by 2030-31. No explicit M&A mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and discounting vs. new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition to remain intense for 1-2 years; company does not match new entrant discounts and benchmarks against the market leader.

qa_highlights.question: Decorative outperformance vs Asian Paints and Berger (8-9% volume growth)?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to premium-led growth, distribution expansion, digital tools and recovery in smaller dealers after new-entrant pressure; no single driver cited.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for July-August?
qa_highlights.answer: July was weaker due to late rains, but management expects Q2 in a similar band and targets double-digit growth in volume and value.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery to the 39.5-40% underlying level as high-cost inventory is consumed; crude-linked raw material costs.
EBITDA margin trajectory versus the 13-15% guidance as headcount and R&D costs continue.
Persistent discounting by new entrants in decorative; mass and economy segment growth lagging.
One-off income (₹55.9 crore dividend, ₹108 crore tax refund) inflates Q1 PAT; underlying profit is lower.
Execution risk in Project Akshaya, ERP migration and exit from AkzoNobel TSA; related-party governance with JSW Paints.

key_quotes: we have decided to reinvest in the growth.

rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity commissioning was discussed; growth is attributed to value per outlet and distribution expansion (active towns ~3,400-3,500 targeted to ~4,500), not capacity additions.

rows.why: Q1 volume grew ~25% (~18-19% after price); management expects Q2 in a similar band despite a weaker July, targeting double-digit volume and value growth.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance held at double-digit volume/value growth and a new 13-15% EBITDA margin band; July weakness from late rains and persistent new-entrant discounting make an upgrade unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 growth guided to a similar band but July was weaker on late rains, and competition from new entrants is expected to persist 1-2 years; margin trajectory versus 13-15% depends on headcount and R&D costs continuing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product or brand launch was named; execution items cited were Velvet Touch and WeatherShield reinforcement and undercoat focus, which are existing products.

rows.label: Project Akshaya synergies with JSW Paints
rows.when: over 3-year roadmap; ₹2.4 crore savings realised in Q1
rows.why: A 3-year roadmap is set and ₹2.4 crore of savings was already realised in Q1, which supports margin recovery alongside input price easing.

rows.why: Being tested in the top 20 towns, with the distributor model retained elsewhere; the active-town target of ~4,500 from ~3,400-3,500 depends on this rollout.

rows.why: Blended inventory is ~95 days against an industry ~110-120 and decorative ~60 days, and lower-cost stock is entering from August, so it is unclear whether further normalisation is planned.

500730|2026-03.headline: NOCIL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 5% QoQ to Rs.330 crore on 7% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.4% amid raw material inflation.
500730|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs.330 crore, up 5% QoQ from Rs.316 crore, with volumes up 7% QoQ, driven by domestic demand after GST 2.0 and steady single-digit international growth. Operating EBITDA fell to Rs.21 crore (6.4% margin) from Rs.27 crore in Q3, hit by gas-driven utility costs, shutdown maintenance and a Rs.7-8 crore inventory-related stock change debit. FY26 revenue fell to Rs.1,303 crore from Rs.1,393 crore, with full-year volumes up 3% and PAT down to Rs.56 crore from Rs.103 crore. Management raised prices on non-contractual business in March and on contractual business from Q1 FY27 in response to sharp raw material inflation linked to Middle East disruption.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes grew single digits QoQ, aided by GST 2.0 demand; management estimates a 100-150 bps market share gain. Volume split FY26 is 70% domestic, 30% exports.

segments.name: International / Exports
segments.commentary: International volumes grew steady single digits in Q4. Export value share is about 33% (67:33 domestic:export by value). US volumes, hit roughly 50% last quarter by duties, are recovering but management expects traction only in FY27.

segments.name: Specialty rubber chemicals
segments.commentary: Specialty is about 15% of mix today, with management targeting about 20% after the new Rs.130 crore integrated specialty facility ramps up.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY26 volume momentum (up 12% YoY) to continue into coming quarters, and says Q4 volumes can serve as the base run rate.
Targets double-digit volume growth in coming years.
Targets EBITDA improvement of about 150 bps from the FY26 base going forward.
Price increases on non-contractual business taken in March and on contractual business from Q1 FY27; management sees the current raw material spike as volatility, not structural demand weakness.
Expects 6-8 months from commissioning before material traction from tyre-based customers on new capacity; non-tyre business should start earlier.
Tax rate reverts to normal rates in FY27 with no specific reduction expected.
capex_capacity: TDQ capex at Dahej (announced 26 March 2024) is complete; trial production has started and samples go to customers for approval. Total capex is under Rs.250 crore.

New Rs.130 crore capex announced 16 March 2026 for a comprehensive integrated specialty rubber chemicals facility at Dahej, expected complete by H1 FY28. Mostly growth capex with some intermediates; largely merchant per management, with a part captive.
Installed capacity cited by analysts at about 1,38,000-1,39,000 tons; management declined to give effective capacity, saying utilisation is roughly 65%.
CWIP was about Rs.220 crore at FY26 end; no project debt drawn yet, with bank lines above Rs.100 crore available at repo-linked rates.
Full-year FY26 capex was largely funded from internal working capital release; analysts estimated Rs.170-180 crore working capital saving.
demand_pricing: Realisations were under pressure from low-priced imports through Q4; management says the market corrected finished goods prices after April input price rises.
About 65-70% of volume is under contract, with the rest non-contractual; roughly 40% of revenue is exposed to anti-dumping products.

DGTR gave positive final findings in March 2026 for antioxidant TDQ and Sulphenamides (CBS and NS), subject to central government approval, which management expects around mid-June (about 90 days). Pilflex 13 and 4ADPA findings are pending, with Pilflex 13 expected within a month or two.
Imports rose in Jan-Feb 2026 YoY; management linked this to FTA routes (Thailand, Korea) and year-end advance-licence imports. The company is pressing the government on FTA value-addition norms.
Management assumes 2-2.5% long-term global rubber demand growth, and 7% domestic demand growth per ICRA.
Competitive intensity is rising from Chinese players in latex, and 6PPD alternatives are at trial stage, with the company working on them.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers negotiating on price or prioritising volume security, and what is the contract mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says talks are positive but weighted to supply reliability; contract share is about 65-70%, with the rest non-contract and repriced first.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA not benefit from inflation given inventory on hand?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy high-cost inventory from the prior year spilled into H1 FY26, and the FTA-driven removal of basic duty on one product compressed spreads. Q4 also had a Rs.7-8 crore stock change debit and March production cuts from gas costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will ADD on TDQ and Sulphenamides lift margins, and what are the timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quantum is premature to assess; the Finance Ministry decision is expected around mid-June, and historically exporters have absorbed duties, so net benefit is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume and mix outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets double-digit volume growth in coming years, with new products adding to volumes gradually through FY27 and not yet material.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs.130 crore project's volume impact and is it merchant?

500780|2026-03.headline: Zuari Industries guides net debt to about INR700 crores by FY26-end, dependent on ~INR850-900 crore Dubai inflows over six months.
500780|2026-03.overview: Sugar operations delivered record crushing of 159.7 lakh quintal and 101.7% capacity utilisation in FY26, with sugar realisation up to INR4,053/quintal from INR3,894. Standalone PAT turned to INR12 crore from a loss of INR37 crore, and consolidated PAT was INR105 crore versus a loss of INR94.4 crore. Management says the St. Regis Dubai project (98% complete, BCC received 21 May 2026) is the main deleveraging lever, with external borrowings of about INR1,900 crore expected to fall to about INR700 crore by year-end. Ethanol remains under pressure from stagnant prices and roughly 100% industry overcapacity, and the Envien bioethanol JV is still stabilising with OMC tenders delayed.

500790|2026-06.headline: Nestlé India says volume growth has been double-digit for recent quarters and ad spend is up ~40%, but gives no numeric FY27 guidance.
500790|2026-06.overview: This was an analyst and investor meet held virtually on 4 August 2026, not a formal Q1 FY27 results call, so no quarterly financial statements were presented. Management said volume-led growth has accelerated over the last four to five quarters, with double-digit volume growth in recent quarters versus a 4.2% five-year volume CAGR. Advertising investment has been raised by close to 40% in recent quarters, which management funds from cost-saving programmes (2.6% of cost base saved in 2025 versus a normal 1.8–1.9%). Management declined to give forward projections, said 40% ad growth will not persist every quarter, and flagged macro headwinds from energy, packaging, oil, shipping and currency.

Normal year 1.8–1.9%; accelerating further this year
From 11%; growing ~500 bps ahead of overall growth

segments.commentary: KITKAT is now India's largest KITKAT market globally for Nestlé; management says the category is among the best performers and capacity was run out, with new capacity being added. Munch new line capex about Rs.225 crore.

segments.commentary: NESCAFÉ recorded its 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. NESPRESSO now has four boutiques in three cities; entry Rs.2 sachets to Rs.100 per espresso pod.

segments.name: Noodles (MAGGI)
segments.commentary: Noodle penetration about 35–36% against ~100% monthly for biscuits; MAGGI is India's largest market globally. New MAGGI line capex about Rs.170 crore in the last calendar year.

segments.name: Dairy and nutrition (LACTOGEN, CERELAC, NAN)
segments.commentary: Management says the segment had good volume-led growth last quarter; CERELAC relaunched with a zero-added-sugar (ZAS) variant alongside the existing sugar-within-limit range. NAN EXCELLAPRO and LACTOGEN with probiotics launched.

segments.name: Pet care (Purina Pro Plan, Felix, Friskies)
segments.commentary: Management says it is gaining cat food share and the category is growing strongly; no revenue figures given.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined forward projections, citing a secular opportunity: noodles penetration ~35–36% versus biscuits ~100%; confectionery shares are small; coffee has 20 quarters of double-digit growth. Acknowledged quarters could be off.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be maintained or modestly improved over the medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Nestlé has a track record of maintaining margins and efficiency programmes support this; management said it is not chasing growth at margin cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ad spend risen 40–50% for three quarters, and what happens to growth when the GST base gets high from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said spend is being raised behind brands with ROAS monitoring; 40% will not continue each quarter; base effects from GST tailwind will show in some quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MPN (nutrition) volume outlook and what initiatives have been added?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no new initiatives beyond the portfolio refresh (CERELAC ZAS variant, NAN EXCELLAPRO, LACTOGEN probiotics) and that volume growth in nutrition is expected to continue; no mid-to-high single-digit target given.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said rural reach is still about half of some peers' level and a long way to go; e-commerce/q-commerce contribution not quantified, with focus on category share rather than absolute growth.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said M&A is not imminent; 9 of 10 focus is on current businesses. Parent-group brands (Pops, Delight, Friskies, NESPRESSO) are being scaled in India.

500800|2026-03.headline: Tata Consumer Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18% to over INR5,400 crores, with EBITDA up 27% and margin expanding 100 bps to 14.6%.
500800|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 18% in Q4 FY26 with India UVG of 16%, and EBITDA grew 27%, lifting margin 100 bps to 14.6%. Full-year revenue crossed INR20,000 crores (up 15%), but full-year EBITDA margin contracted to 13.9% after a soft first half on high tea and US coffee costs. India tea was price-cut as tea costs fell, with tea margins now back to the target range. Management guided to 50-75 bps full-year margin expansion in FY27, double-digit top-line growth, and a stepped-up A&P ratio of 7.5-8.5%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said packaging and LPG costs have risen, but margins have not been hit materially so far. It is confident of EBITDA growing ahead of revenue and 50-75 bps full-year expansion, with pricing as a mitigation lever.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Sampann grow nearly 70%, and can its margin match the beverage and salt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was broad-based across pulses, poha and vermicelli, helped by NPDs and quick-commerce/e-commerce reach. Sampann is heading to a mid-teens margin after promotion and advertising; salt is strong and beverages have recovered.

qa_highlights.answer: Management wants a higher tea volume number than 4% and aspires to beat mid-single-digit volume. Quick commerce is treated as the consumer-first channel where it can test and scale before rolling out to modern trade and general trade.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tea cost outlook for FY27 and will tea margins expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Tea costs are roughly flat year-on-year; the season started with auctions up in April. Q4 tea margins are roughly where management wants them, and it will react with pricing to commodity moves.

qa_highlights.answer: Capital Foods was hit by the nationwide go-to-market relaunch in top cities between November and February, plus March shipping disruption via the Middle East. Organic India benefited from onshore US inventory built up earlier.

500800|2026-06.headline: Tata Consumer Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12% to INR5,349 crore, with EBITDA up 19% and margin at 13.6%, up 70 bps.
500800|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 12% to INR5,349 crore (9% in constant currency), with India business UVG of 13%. EBITDA grew 19% and margin expanded 70 bps to 13.6%, while net profit rose 29% to INR427 crore (reported EPS INR4.31; adjusted EPS INR4.67). Growth businesses grew 47% and reached 36% of revenue, with Sampann, RTD and Capital Foods/Organic India leading. India tea revenue fell 4% despite 2% volume growth as tea prices were passed on, and India margins compressed sequentially on inflation, staggered pricing, higher A&P and FX losses.

segments.name: India salt
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7% on 7% volume growth despite June price increase (Tata Salt orange bag MRP INR30 to INR32); value-added salt grew 13%; market share close to 39%.

segments.name: India tea and coffee
segments.commentary: Revenue down 4% to INR1,200 crore as tea prices were passed on; tea volume +2%, coffee +24%. Unusually long summer and LPG shortage hit small restaurants and tea stalls in the south.

segments.name: Sampann and growth portfolio
segments.commentary: Sampann revenue +58%, volume-led; core pulses/spices/poha/vermicelli growing about 30%, with cold-pressed oil and dry fruits adding to growth. Sampann margin up 150-200 bps YoY.

segments.name: RTD (water and beverages)
segments.commentary: Revenue +41% on 38% volume growth; Tata Water Plus volumes up 35% with revenue +41%. Kombucha Zero launched in two variants.

segments.name: Capital Foods and Organic India
segments.commentary: Capital Foods INR232 crore (+40%); Organic India INR118 crore (+27%); combined gross margin close to 50%. Tata Soulfull grew 45%.

segments.name: International (incl. Starbucks India)
segments.commentary: Constant currency +3%, reported +16%. US +7% constant currency (seventh straight quarter of share gains); UK and Canada hit by warm weather; Starbucks revenue +11%. Non-branded and solubles/plantation declined on lower coffee prices.

Management reiterated double-digit consolidated revenue growth as the norm, with some quarters at mid-teens and others at low double digits.
Medium-term aspiration: good India food business at 17-20% EBITDA margin; tea and salt gross margin 33-36%.

Management is evaluating bringing scale categories in-house; manufacturing capex for these categories is described as not heavy.
Water distribution reach about 40-50% of the 75% of the country where it is available; North and West are described as white space.
demand_pricing: Tea: input cost inflation of 7-10% seen so far, mainly at the lower end of the portfolio; pricing taken in June, with more to follow if inflation persists; buying is still early.

Coffee: lower coffee prices helped the branded US business; the non-branded business is pass-through, so management calls the net effect positive.
Pulses: management expects to pass on any price rise; Sampann pulses about INR600-700 crore in a INR2.2 lakh crore pulses market with 6% branded penetration.
Non-branded business was down 10% constant currency; solubles down 12% and plantation down 8%.
Management says it has gained market share in tea in relative terms over the last couple of years, although Nielsen disclosure has been stopped.

qa_highlights.question: Whether growth businesses can invest in own capacity, pass on cost inflation in spices, dry fruits and edible oil, and reach a 35% growth norm for Capital Foods and Organic India.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most Capital Foods and Organic India production is in-house, and inflation will be passed on with a time lag. It set the Capital Foods and Organic India norm at 25-30% growth, with the go-to-market reset completed in February.

qa_highlights.question: Why India margins fell sequentially while international margins rose.
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Goenka cited input cost inflation, a timing gap between cost hikes and staggered pricing, higher A&P, and FX losses on hedges in India. International margins benefited from lower US coffee prices.

qa_highlights.question: Tea pricing outlook and inflation.
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil D'Souza said tea inflation is 7-10% so far, with buying still early; pricing will be reviewed after 15-30 days and taken up if needed to protect margins.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of margin expansion beyond salt pricing, and the path toward a 20% margin.
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers listed were full pricing impact, US coffee normalisation, cost saving drives, mix shift to Capital Foods and Organic India, water utilisation gains and operating leverage, with Sampann margins close to 12%.

qa_highlights.answer: Starbucks same-store sales grew mid-single digit; with new stores, management expects high single-digit top-line growth. Tea volume is guided at mid-single digit.

El Nino and erratic monsoon, plus lower pulse sowing, which could raise prices in pulses and tea.

Sequential India margin compression: management says the Q1 India EBITDA margin dip is timing-related and expects it to recover.

500800|2026-09.headline: Tata Consumer Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% to about INR4,000+ crores-equivalent run rate; EBITDA up 18%, margin up 40 bps to 14%, net profit INR470 crores (+16%).
500800|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% (INR700 crores added), EBITDA grew 18% with margin up 40 bps to 14%, and profit before tax rose 21%. Net profit reached INR470 crores (+16%), EPS INR4.75; adjusted EPS (excluding brand amortisation) was INR5.18. First half revenue grew 13%, EBITDA 18%, and adjusted EPS INR9.85 (+21%). India business grew 11% UVG in the quarter, with salt (+15% revenue) and growth businesses (+40%) offsetting flat tea/coffee revenue (-1%); India segment margin contracted on tea and salt input inflation. International (+7% reported, -2% constant currency) and non-branded (+12%) improved profitability, lifting overall segment margin by 50 bps; shipping disruption and Mundra port issue hit international volumes. Management reiterated FY27 margin expansion guidance of 50-70 bps and said tea and salt price increases should flow into P&L from Q3.

500820|2026-03.headline: Asian Paints Q4 FY26 decorative volume grew 12.4% and standalone PBDIT rose 26%, with management reiterating an 18-20% margin guidance despite roughly 10.5-11% cumulative price hikes.
500820|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: decorative volume grew 12.4% and value 10.2%, with all three months double-digit and volume-value gap narrowing to about 2.2%. Standalone net sales rose 10.3% and PBDIT 26% to a 21.2% margin, while gross margin reached about 45.6% on deflation of roughly 1.4%. Management has taken about 10.5-11% price increases, flagged further calibrated hikes and expects high single-digit to 8-10% volume growth ahead, while it says competitive discounting remains intense. Full-year FY26 standalone net sales grew 4.3% and consolidated 5.1%, with a 60% dividend payout (total Rs 27.5 per share).

500825|2026-03.headline: Britannia Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7.1% to INR 4,686 crore, with PAT up 21.1% to INR 678 crore helped by a tax case release.
500825|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 4,686 crore (+7.1% YoY) and FY26 revenue was INR 18,858 crore (+7.5%). Q4 PAT of INR 678 crore (+21.1%) was lifted by income tax case closures, so underlying profit growth was weaker. Management attributed the India slowdown in March to dual pricing of INR 5 and INR 10 packs after the GST transition, which hit wholesale and rural channels, plus West Asia disruption to international dispatches. Management guided to price increases from this quarter to offset fuel and laminate inflation.

financial_highlights.change: +21.1% YoY; 14.5% of revenue; boosted by income tax case releases

segments.name: Domestic India
segments.commentary: Growth was about 9% to 9.5% in Q4 before dual-pricing drag; management said it expects a few hundred bps of lost sales to recover. Retail (75% of business) is growing well, while wholesale (25%) was hit.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce was 6% of domestic sales in FY26 versus 4% in FY25, and management put it above 12% excluding the INR 5 and INR 10 packs. Quick commerce is about 70% of e-commerce, which management expects to reach 85%.

segments.name: International (West Asia)
segments.commentary: Revenue and profitability were hit in Q4 by vessel unavailability through the Strait of Hormuz and weaker demand in West Asia markets. Management said the business was negative for March, and Oman production for North America has moved back to Mundra.

segments.name: Adjacencies and signature brands
segments.commentary: Wafers are growing at healthy double digits and dairy at double digits, led by ghee. Treat, Little Hearts and Jim Jam are growing about 3x company growth, and cake and rusk is growing about 1.4x biscuits.

guidance_outlook: Calibrated price increases start from Q1 FY27, through grammage adjustments and some packs above INR 10.
Management expects the domestic market to stabilize by quarter-end as dual pricing fades, and expects wholesale and rural volumes to recover.
Sourcing optimisation between India and international plants is expected to be fully operational by mid-May 2026.
Management expects biscuit industry sequential growth to resume from June with monsoon and school reopening.
Management is committed to continued cost efficiency programmes (CEP) and plans to step up advertising and brand investment, with no quantified FY27 margin guidance.
No specific FY27 revenue or margin number was given; management said it is confident of a good year.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing for North America was moved from Oman back to Mundra, enabling dispatch to North America.
Management is evaluating alternate fuels and energy sources as long-term hedges against fuel supply shocks.
Renewable electricity share in own plants rose 14%, and specific water consumption fell 7%.
Management did not announce new capacity or capex figures.
demand_pricing: Dual pricing of INR 5 and INR 10 packs (competitor selling at INR 4.5 and INR 9) hit rural and wholesale channels from January through March; the 60-65% of biscuits sold at these price points are most exposed.
Management said the gap is about 200 to 400 bps in sales, but it cannot precisely quantify the impact.
Price realisation on the INR 5 and INR 10 segment is lower than the competitor's, so management believes value share is unaffected.

Raw material view: wheat is deflationary but has risen over the past month on rains and quality; palm oil is covered for 5 months; sugar stable; cocoa lower; laminate and fuel (LPG, CNG) are inflationary.
Wheat inventory is covered for about 5.5 to 6 months at attractive prices; palm oil is covered for 5 months.
Other expenses rose 18% on 7% revenue growth, driven by higher advertising and brand investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why was standalone growth lower in Q4 when Nov-Dec ran at about 12% and Jan-Feb at about 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first two months of Q4 were reasonable, with dual pricing in rural and wholesale channels hitting throughout the quarter, and West Asia pulling March down. Domestic growth was about 9% to 9.5% before the dual-pricing drag.

qa_highlights.question: How much did dual pricing dampen sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was hypothetical to quantify, but the impact was roughly 200 to 400 bps. Growth in general trade key accounts is high-single to double digit, modern trade is about 15% to 16%, and e-commerce is above 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What pricing action is needed given competitors are vacating INR 4.5 and INR 9 packs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will take selective price increases through grammage adjustments and some packs above INR 10. Other biscuit companies are moving gradually to full price points.

qa_highlights.question: Is Britannia under-indexed on INR 5 and INR 10 packs in e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not actively promote these packs online because premium packs drive more value and channel conflict is a concern. The packs remain available through search and in baskets.

qa_highlights.question: Will GST cut benefits reach biscuits, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the GST benefit is less visible on INR 5 and INR 10 packs than on higher price points. It expects benefits to show more in medium to long term, with the growth recovery in June.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q4 volume growth and how do pack counts look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth was about 5.5% by grammage. It acknowledged that transactions fell in wholesale and rural channels and expects this to correct over the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 given cost pressures and higher investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will be selective on marketing spend, targeting the marketing mix for better returns, and expects to manage margins within a certain band. No quantified FY27 margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue inorganic growth and new platforms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is actively scanning acquisitions that add new capabilities or address unmet needs, and that more platforms will be added, including health.

risks_watch: Recovery of dual-pricing-hit wholesale and rural channels and whether the INR 5 and INR 10 price points normalise.
Q4 PAT includes income tax case releases, so the reported 21.1% PAT growth is not recurring.
Fuel and laminate inflation, plus West Asia shipping and LPG constraints, could pressure margins and international operations.
Competitor (number 2 player) reported double-digit volume growth, which may signal share loss in INR 5 and INR 10 channels.
Rising other expenses (+18% YoY) from brand investment could weigh on margins in FY27.
Price increases could affect volumes, which management argues will remain resilient.
500825|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on medium-term recovery and cost discipline, but cautious and sometimes vague on near-term numbers. Management avoided quantifying the dual-pricing impact and FY27 guidance, and said the outcome depends on execution.

And we are very confident that in very short period of time, these channels will also come back to normalcy.
So we had a volume growth of close to 5.5% upwards.

500825|2026-06.headline: Britannia Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 9.5% to INR 4,964 crore, with ~9% tonnage volume growth and PAT margin at 11.9%.
500825|2026-06.overview: Management said revenue from operations on a consolidated basis was about INR 4,964 crore, up 9.5% YoY, with standalone growth at 10%. PAT was 11.9% of revenue and grew 13.6% YoY. Management said the quarter exited in mid-teens growth after dual-pricing disruption in rural and wholesale channels faded in June. Input cost inflation from LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar and milk is a headwind, and management said only about half of it has been offset through price increases so far.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 52 crore last year, as stated by an analyst
none booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27

segments.name: General Trade (GT)
segments.commentary: Management said GT demand picked up, with the recent run-rate about 1.5x the full-year FY26 growth rate. Key states are growing and other states are growing about 1.3x faster.

segments.name: E-commerce / Quick commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce grew at strong double digits. Quick commerce is about 80-85% of e-commerce and is growing at healthy double digits.

segments.name: Other channels
segments.commentary: Newer channels were growing at about 2.5x the GT rate overall.

segments.name: Dairy and adjacencies
segments.commentary: Dairy grew at double digits. Cake, rusk and wafers grew at double digits led by portfolio innovation. Croissant lines were growing above 30% and Croissant run-rate was about INR 200 crore annualised (INR 100 crore ARR doubled).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Mixed quarter: pressure in Middle East and Saudi Arabia and headwinds in North America, offset by growth in Africa led by Kenya. Management expects a return to growth from this quarter.

segments.name: Eastern India
segments.commentary: Growing in double digits per management.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give explicit FY27 guidance. It said the team is confident of a good year, defined as balanced growth across volume, value and profitability.
Management expects roughly 1.5-2% more price realisation from shrinkflation changes to come through in the coming quarters, after about 1% in Q1.
Management said it is watching sugar, palm oil, milk and LPG/PNG costs ahead of the festive season and said the current cost level is higher than in February 2026.
Management said Q2 faces a base effect in September from the GST price transition last year, and July and August were normal months.
Brand-building spend is running ahead of sales growth, with no percentage given.
capex_capacity: Management said it is working to reduce LPG/PNG dependence through biomass and alternate fuels, but no timelines were given.
Renewable energy share in plant power rose 16%, and management is working to expand it under state rules.
A new Chief Business Officer for Dairy was appointed and a Strategy and Corporate Development head joined, with management saying the leadership team is now complete.
demand_pricing: Q1 volume growth was about 9% in tonnage terms; pricing contributed about 1% and was mainly shrinkflation in INR 5 and INR 10 packs.
Management said dual pricing disruption in rural and wholesale was felt in April and early May and ended in June. Demand was described as holding up.
Industrial fuel inflation was steep: LPG and PNG roughly 2.5x in April-May, now about 1.5x February levels. Palm oil is near INR 140 per kg, up more than 20%.
Management said it could mitigate about half of input inflation through price increases so far.
Sugar rose more than INR 7 per kg in the last 2-3 weeks. Flour has held up, but El Nino and rainfall are a watch item for wheat prices.
Management said it has regained market share on a sequential basis across many biscuit categories, following the end of dual pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the mid-teens exit growth in June, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company sells in based on sell-out, so no loading. The dual-pricing impact ended in June, which brought back some buyers, and organic demand held up. It gave no forward indication.

qa_highlights.question: How will ad spend and input inflation affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LPG prices are about 1.5x February levels and sugar and palm oil are also up. Brand spend is ahead of sales growth, with no percentage given. Management said half of inflation has been offset by price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 EBITDA margin hold at or above FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the input cost base is higher than in February. It did not commit to full-year margins, but said it is confident of managing levers across value, volume and margin.

qa_highlights.question: Are there PLI benefits in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no PLI incentive was booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27, because the threshold growth was not achieved.

qa_highlights.question: How is Britannia responding to GT competition in Eastern India and other areas?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited regional empowerment, targeted media and influencer spend, and local product innovation such as Milk Bikis Thirukkural packs in Tamil Nadu. Sub-distributors are being converted to direct distributors.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the GST impact on volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said over 60% of sales are at INR 5 and INR 10 price points, so GST-cut elasticity will be gradual and smaller than for higher-priced packs.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar and milk, with festive-season sugar pressure and monsoon/El Nino risk to wheat and flour.
Margin pressure from higher brand spend and only partial pass-through of input costs (about half so far).

500830|2026-03.headline: Colgate India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% to Rs 1,583 crore, with domestic growth at 9.2% and gross margin at 69.6%.

Full-year FY26 sales were flat at Rs 5,984 crore, and full-year EBITDA margin was 31.2% including an 80 bps GST input-credit (IDS) impact. Q4 NPAT was Rs 353 crore, and excluding one-offs (restructuring, GST, prior-period tax refunds, labour code) management said profit grew about 9%. Management declared an interim dividend of Rs 48 per share and said it is still paying out virtually 100% of NPAT.

500840|2026-03.headline: EIH Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue up 10% but EBITDA up only 1% on business mix, wage code and higher expenses; FY26 PAT hit by Rs 30 Cr wage code charge.
500840|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a very volatile year (Operation Sindoor, West Asia conflict, monsoon rains, December flight disruptions, late-February West Asia war) but said EBITDA was the highest in company history. Q4 consolidated revenue grew 10% while EBITDA grew 1%, with profit from operations down 5% on higher tax expense, business mix shift toward lower-margin OFS (flight catering), higher airport levy, repair and maintenance, CSR, legal and donation costs. For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 8% and EBITDA 3%; reported PAT fell on a one-time Rs 30 Cr wage code impact and the Mashobra fair-value charge from the prior year, and management said excluding these profit grew 2%. Management said April and May trends were better than expected, led by domestic demand.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give forward numbers; said April and May were better than expected, led by strong domestic demand.
Foreign business (about 50% of Q4 business historically) hit by West Asia war; management expects the impact to be limited in summer months, with foreign travel peaking October to March.
Management expects a big summit in Q2 and Q3 FY27 to benefit demand, following AI Summit benefit in February-March.
Capex of about Rs 600-700 Cr a year to continue for the next one to two years, rising in FY29-30 when larger hotels open.
Oberoi Grand Kolkata partial opening still targeted for September 2026; Trident Vizag opens 2027; 825 owned/associate keys and 1,893 managed keys in pipeline by 2030.
Mashobra hotel O&M continues until October 2026; management awaits further developments.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about Rs 680 Cr: about Rs 330 Cr on Mumbai land conversion (leasehold to freehold), Rs 125 Cr on Oberoi Rajgarh, about Rs 100 Cr on ongoing renovations (Kolkata and others), remainder replacement capex.
Oberoi Rajgarh opened November 2025, total 3,800 keys in business with Rajgarh added in Q3; about 400 international keys.

Pipeline: 825 owned/associate keys by 2030, starting with Trident Vizag (2027) via EIH Associated Hotels; Hebbal mixed-use site (about 1.3 million sq ft development, including about 7.6 lakh sq ft commercial) by 2030.
Managed pipeline: 24 hotels, 1,893 keys; two new Trident management contracts added (Amritsar, 150 keys; Pawna, 150 keys), signed between Q3 and Q4.

Oberoi Grand Kolkata (about 200 keys) renovation under way with structural works; reopening targeted September 2026. Oberoi Grand Kolkata cited as timeline issue; separately, Oberoi Gandikota site delay moved from 2028 to 2030 due to site change.

Renovations: about 90 rooms at Oberoi Bangalore in 18-room blocks over summer; Trident Nariman Point 4 floors (six months); 4 floors at Oberoi Mumbai one floor at a time; F&B overhaul at Trident Bandra Kurla later in FY27.
demand_pricing: Q4 industry occupancy 67-69%, below last year on West Asia war impact; industry ARR up 6-8% and RevPAR up 5-7%. FY26 industry occupancy flat, ARR up 9-10%, RevPAR up 10-12%.

Occupancy weakened through Q4 with a sharp drop in March; ARR for EIH owned hotels rose from Rs 24,548 to Rs 28,198 in Q4. January RevPAR negative (about -6%), which management attributed to unexplained weak demand, possibly negative international press on air quality.
Delhi/NCR, Mumbai (T20 World Cup) and Bhubaneswar grew strongly; Bangalore hit by lower foreign bookings; Udaipur down on fewer weddings.
Room revenue: MICE and direct segments grew; corporate and leisure flat.
Management says India is significantly underpriced versus Europe, North America and parts of Asia at the top end; no reason to discount rates given rate premium strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What drove February ARR growth near 25% and why was January RevPAR negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said January was weak, with promotions having limited effect; the likely cause (unvalidated) was negative international press on North India air quality. February was strong, helped by the AI Summit, deferred winter travel and strong demand across leisure and city hotels.

qa_highlights.question: With few owned key additions in FY27-28, what drives growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Two levers: ARR (premium positioning, headroom if market stays buoyant) and cost elimination of waste rather than cuts. No specific growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 flight catering (OFS) revenue and was it new clients?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 145 Cr in Q4, mainly existing airlines expanding flights and market share, including some domestic airlines.

qa_highlights.question: Where do foreign tourist mix and Q4 FTA levels stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 foreign business about 50% historically; domestic share rose substantially in March and more than offset weaker foreign demand. Exact March quarter mix to be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a financial loss from geopolitical issues in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: No financial impact calculated; lower foreign room nights were offset by domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 20% in Q4 and will Mashobra O&M continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher expenses from business growth, higher airport levy on OFS, higher R&M, CSR, legal and donation costs. Mashobra case settled in June; hotel operated until October 2026.

risks_watch: Margin pressure: Q4 EBITDA only 1% growth as OFS mix rises and airport levy and wage code costs increase; watch for margin recovery in FY27.
Managed hotel project slippage (Trident Goa, Dehradun, Rishikesh and others); management says owners control timelines and delays are not significant, but 2027 pipeline looks thin.
Oberoi Grand Kolkata renovation: structural issues found, reopening target September 2026 still stated; any change would be updated to the board and investors.
Oberoi Rajgarh (Khajuraho) connectivity: only seasonal Delhi flights; no flights expected July-September unless IndiGo extends.
Geopolitical risk: West Asia war impact on foreign travel and occupancy; the company has not quantified the impact; March occupancy weakness may persist into Q1 FY27.
Supply risk in FY29-30 from new luxury keys in some micro-markets; management says the rate premium will be maintained rather than discounted.
500840|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and pipeline but cautious on near-term occupancy; management acknowledged a challenging year and avoided forward numbers, deferring several specifics (foreign mix, flight catering split, consolidated room revenue) to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: But that's not to undermine the fact that we had challenges in the year .
So, the full year occupancy for our own hotels was 76.8 or 77% for the year.
So overall, if you look at our investor update, we've almost spent 600 to 700 crores of CAPEX in the current year.
Foreign travel really picks up in October through to March , and with April being somewhat strong, maybe not as strong as the winter months, but still reasonable.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Room revenue growth is supported by Trident RevPAR up 10.2% and Oberoi RevPAR up 10.4% in FY26 versus the market, April-May trends better than expected, and OFS volumes rising with existing airlines adding flights, offset by foreign weakness and a negative January RevPAR of about -6%.
